people.summary: Born 21 October 1872 and baptised at Ward End, Aston, on 19 June 1873, son of William and Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice. An engineer all his working life. He married Edith Madeline Spencer at St Matthew's, Brixton, on 2 August 1897. Their son Baron Reginald was baptised at the Ascension, Balham Hill, on 21 August 1904. He lived in Cape Town from 1916 to about 1923. He died on 7 June 1928, probably aged 55, and was buried at Chingford Mount. He was not a son of the Earls of Orkney.
people.story:
Edward Dixon FitzMaurice was born on 21 October 1872 and baptised on 19 June 1873 at St Margaret's, Ward End, Aston. The register names his parents as William and Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice, of Ward End, and his father as a surveyor and contractor.[^parish-wardend-1873] His own marriage register names that father as Robert William Fitzmaurice, a contractor.[^parish-brixton-1897] The birth index gives his mother's maiden name as Falcke.[^gro-indexes] In 1881 he is the boy written as Ernest Dixon, aged 8, born at Little Bromwich, in the household of Robert William FitzMaurice and Fanny Mary at Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston]

In 1891 he was an apprentice civil engineer, a lodger at 25 Compton Avenue, Brighton, born at Ward End.[^census-1891-brighton] On 2 August 1897, aged 25 and a professional singer, he married Edith Madeline Spencer at St Matthew's, Brixton, by banns.[^parish-brixton-1897] He was probably a civil mechanical engineer in Brixton in 1901.[^census-1901-brixton] On 21 August 1904, described as a civil engineer of 29 Cathles Road, he and Edith Madeline had their son Baron Reginald baptised at the Ascension, Balham Hill.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg] In 1911 he was a civil engineer at Whitstable, with Edith and three children.[^census-1911-whitstable]

In the middle of the First World War, by then a civil engineer of about 43, he sailed from London for South Africa on the Balmoral Castle on 29 March 1916, meaning to settle there.[^passenger-1916-balmoral] Five months later Edith probably followed on the Llanstephan Castle with Bob, Reg and Eileen.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] He came back to England in October 1923, giving Whitstable as his address, and sailed for Cape Town again that December.[^passenger-1923-armadale] [^passenger-1923-arundel] Edith came home in November 1925.[^passenger-1925-edith]

He died on 7 June 1928, probably aged 55, and was buried at Chingford Mount Cemetery.[^findagrave-214209661] [^burial-chingford-1928] When Eileen married in 1936, the paper remembered him as formerly of Cape Town.[^news-1936-simmons]

Edward was an engineer all his working life: an apprentice civil engineer in 1891, a civil engineer in 1901 and 1911, and an engineer on every passenger list from 1916 to 1923. The white collar in the beach photo is not a sign that he was a clergyman.[^beach-snapshots]

He was not a son of the Hon. Henry Warrender FitzMaurice. The London Gazette of 23 April 1890 names the 7th Earl of Orkney's surviving brother and sister, and Edward is not among them.[^gazette-1890]

people.summary_de: Geboren am 21. Oktober 1872 und getauft in Ward End, Aston, am 19. Juni 1873, Sohn von William und Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice. Sein ganzes Arbeitsleben lang Ingenieur. Er heiratete Edith Madeline Spencer am 2. August 1897 in St Matthew's, Brixton. Ihr Sohn Baron Reginald wurde am 21. August 1904 in der Ascension, Balham Hill, getauft. Er lebte von 1916 bis etwa 1923 in Kapstadt. Er starb am 7. Juni 1928, wahrscheinlich im Alter von 55 Jahren, und wurde in Chingford Mount beigesetzt. Er war kein Sohn der Earls of Orkney.
people.story_de:
Edward Dixon FitzMaurice wurde am 21. Oktober 1872 geboren und am 19. Juni 1873 in St Margaret's, Ward End, Aston, getauft. Das Register nennt seine Eltern als William und Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice aus Ward End und seinen Vater als Vermesser und Bauunternehmer.[^parish-wardend-1873] Sein eigenes Heiratsregister nennt diesen Vater als Robert William Fitzmaurice, einen Bauunternehmer.[^parish-brixton-1897] Der Geburtsindex gibt den Mädchennamen seiner Mutter als Falcke an.[^gro-indexes] 1881 ist er der Junge, der als Ernest Dixon eingetragen ist, 8 Jahre alt, geboren in Little Bromwich, im Haushalt von Robert William FitzMaurice und Fanny Mary in Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston]

1891 war er Lehrling als Bauingenieur und Untermieter in 25 Compton Avenue, Brighton, geboren in Ward End.[^census-1891-brighton] Am 2. August 1897, 25 Jahre alt und Berufssänger, heiratete er Edith Madeline Spencer in St Matthew's, Brixton, nach Aufgebot.[^parish-brixton-1897] 1901 war er in Brixton wahrscheinlich Bau- und Maschinenbauingenieur.[^census-1901-brixton] Am 21. August 1904, bezeichnet als Bauingenieur von 29 Cathles Road, ließen er und Edith Madeline ihren Sohn Baron Reginald in der Ascension, Balham Hill, taufen.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg] 1911 war er Bauingenieur in Whitstable, mit Edith und drei Kindern.[^census-1911-whitstable]

Mitten im Ersten Weltkrieg, inzwischen Bauingenieur von etwa 43 Jahren, fuhr er am 29. März 1916 von London auf der Balmoral Castle nach Südafrika, mit der Absicht, sich dort niederzulassen.[^passenger-1916-balmoral] Fünf Monate später folgte Edith wahrscheinlich auf der Llanstephan Castle mit Bob, Reg und Eileen.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] Im Oktober 1923 kam er nach England zurück, gab Whitstable als Adresse an und fuhr im Dezember erneut nach Kapstadt.[^passenger-1923-armadale] [^passenger-1923-arundel] Edith kam im November 1925 nach Hause.[^passenger-1925-edith]

Er starb am 7. Juni 1928, wahrscheinlich im Alter von 55 Jahren, und wurde auf dem Chingford Mount Cemetery beigesetzt.[^findagrave-214209661] [^burial-chingford-1928] Als Eileen 1936 heiratete, erinnerte die Zeitung an ihn als ehemals aus Kapstadt.[^news-1936-simmons]

Edward war sein ganzes Arbeitsleben lang Ingenieur: 1891 Lehrling als Bauingenieur, 1901 und 1911 Bauingenieur und auf jeder Passagierliste von 1916 bis 1923 Ingenieur. Der weiße Kragen auf dem Strandfoto ist kein Zeichen dafür, dass er Geistlicher war.[^beach-snapshots]

Er war kein Sohn des Hon. Henry Warrender FitzMaurice. Die London Gazette vom 23. April 1890 nennt den überlebenden Bruder und die überlebende Schwester des 7. Earl of Orkney, und Edward ist nicht darunter.[^gazette-1890]

people.summary: Reg's mother, not his sister. Edith Madeline Spencer married Edward Dixon FitzMaurice on 2 August 1897. She was probably born about 1866 to 1869 in Islington. She probably died in the Bridge district of Kent in early 1929, aged 61. She was probably in South Africa from about 1916 to 1925.
people.story:
The medallion portrait inscribed Edith Madeleine Fitzmaurice, about 1899, is Edith Madeline Spencer, Edward Dixon's wife and Reg's mother. Earlier pages that called her Reg's sister were wrong.[^edith-medallion] [^parish-brixton-1897]

She was probably born about 1866 to 1869 in Islington. In 1891 she was 22, a governess, born in Islington, living with her widowed mother Caroline at 15 Mornington Place, St Pancras. The house number may read 15b.[^census-1891-spencer] Her death in 1929, aged 61, fits that birth. At the wedding she was recorded as 24, and in 1911 as 38 and born at St Anne, Soho. Those later ages are the odd ones out. Her birth registration has not been found. A birth of Edith Maria Spencer at Islington in 1866 belongs to a different family and is not hers.[^census-1891-spencer] [^gro-edith-death] [^census-1911-whitstable]

On 2 August 1897 she married Edward at St Matthew's, Brixton. Her father, Charles Spencer, a builder and contractor, was already dead. Caroline Spencer was a witness.[^parish-brixton-1897] In 1911, at Whitstable, she and Edward had had four children, of whom three were living. The child who had died was Edith Marjorie.[^census-1911-whitstable] She probably died in the March quarter of 1929 in the Bridge district of Kent, aged 61.[^gro-edith-death]

She probably went out to Cape Town in August 1916 with Bob, Reg and Eileen. At the end of 1923 she came to London with Reg and Eileen on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, and gave 140A Clapham Road, London S.W. (the number is hard to read).[^passenger-1923-bendigo] She came back to England from South Africa in November 1925, aged 53 by her own account, giving Birkenhead as her destination.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] [^passenger-1925-edith]

In August 1904 she and Edward were living at 29 Cathles Road, Balham Hill, when their son Baron Reginald was baptised at the Ascension, Balham Hill.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg]

people.summary_de: Regs Mutter, nicht seine Schwester. Edith Madeline Spencer heiratete Edward Dixon FitzMaurice am 2. August 1897. Sie wurde wahrscheinlich etwa 1866 bis 1869 in Islington geboren. Sie starb wahrscheinlich Anfang 1929 im Bezirk Bridge in Kent, im Alter von 61 Jahren. Sie war wahrscheinlich von etwa 1916 bis 1925 in Südafrika.
people.story_de:
Das Medaillonporträt mit der Aufschrift Edith Madeleine Fitzmaurice, etwa 1899, ist Edith Madeline Spencer, die Ehefrau von Edward Dixon und Regs Mutter. Frühere Seiten, die sie Regs Schwester nannten, lagen falsch.[^edith-medallion] [^parish-brixton-1897]

Sie wurde wahrscheinlich etwa 1866 bis 1869 in Islington geboren. 1891 war sie 22, Gouvernante, geboren in Islington, und lebte mit ihrer verwitweten Mutter Caroline in 15 Mornington Place, St Pancras. Die Hausnummer könnte 15b lauten.[^census-1891-spencer] Ihr Tod 1929 im Alter von 61 Jahren passt zu dieser Geburt. Bei der Hochzeit wurde sie als 24 geführt, 1911 als 38 und geboren in St Anne, Soho. Diese späteren Altersangaben fallen aus dem Rahmen. Ihre Geburtsregistrierung wurde nicht gefunden. Eine Geburt von Edith Maria Spencer in Islington 1866 gehört zu einer anderen Familie und ist nicht ihre.[^census-1891-spencer] [^gro-edith-death] [^census-1911-whitstable]

Am 2. August 1897 heiratete sie Edward in St Matthew's, Brixton. Ihr Vater, Charles Spencer, Baumeister und Bauunternehmer, war bereits tot. Caroline Spencer war Zeugin.[^parish-brixton-1897] 1911 in Whitstable hatten sie und Edward vier Kinder gehabt, von denen drei lebten. Das gestorbene Kind war Edith Marjorie.[^census-1911-whitstable] Sie starb wahrscheinlich im März-Quartal 1929 im Bezirk Bridge in Kent, im Alter von 61 Jahren.[^gro-edith-death]

Wahrscheinlich reiste sie im August 1916 mit Bob, Reg und Eileen nach Kapstadt. Ende 1923 kam sie mit Reg und Eileen auf der Bendigo nach London, landete am 28. Dezember 1923 und gab 140A Clapham Road, London S.W. an (die Nummer ist schwer zu lesen).[^passenger-1923-bendigo] Im November 1925 kam sie aus Südafrika nach England zurück, nach ihrer eigenen Angabe 53 Jahre alt, und nannte Birkenhead als Ziel.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] [^passenger-1925-edith]

Im August 1904 wohnten sie und Edward in 29 Cathles Road, Balham Hill, als ihr Sohn Baron Reginald in der Ascension, Balham Hill, getauft wurde.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg]

people.summary: The oldest photograph in the collection, a carte de visite from J. Perriman of Camden Town. Neither sitter is named, and the card does not show where the family came from.
people.story:
The oldest photograph in the collection is a carte de visite of a seated woman and a young girl. The back is stamped J. Perriman, Camden Town School of Photography, 3 Greenland Place, side of the Mother Red Cap, number 925.[^perriman-cdv] The dress and the format look like the late 1860s or the 1870s.[^genealogy-report]

Neither sitter is named. The card does not establish a North London home for this family. Edward Dixon's parents married at Battersea, and their children were born at Birmingham.[^parish-battersea-1861] [^census-1881-aston]

people.summary: Pat's father. Baron is his forename, not a title. He was baptised on 21 August 1904 at the Ascension, Balham Hill, the son of Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline Fitzmaurice. He was probably born on 26 May 1904 in the Wandsworth district. He probably married Lilian Maud Mary Bennett in late 1927. He died on 31 March 1977.
people.story:
Reg was Baron Reginald FitzMaurice. Baron is a forename, not a title. He was probably born on 26 May 1904 in the Wandsworth district. The birth index names his mother as Spenser, a spelling of Spencer, volume 1d, page 670.[^gro-indexes] [^probate-reg-1977] He was baptised on 21 August 1904 at the parish of the Ascension, Balham Hill, entry 604, page 76. The register names him Baron Reginald, son of Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline Fitzmaurice, of 29 Cathles Road, and his father as a civil engineer. No date of birth is written in the register.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg] In 1911 he is Baron Reginald, aged 6, at school, in Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline's household at Whitstable.[^census-1911-whitstable]

He probably married Lilian Maud Mary Bennett in the December quarter of 1927, in the Hammersmith district, volume 1a, page 661.[^gro-marriage-1927] Electoral registers place him in Wandsworth in 1925 and 1926, Hammersmith from 1931 to 1933, the Spelthorne district from 1934 to 1937, and Hayes from 1938 until about 1972.[^electoral-fitzmaurice] On 11 February 1950 he gave his daughter Patricia away at St Mary's, Wanstead. The album calls him Mr R. Fitzmaurice of Hayes.[^album-1950]

He died on 31 March 1977. The death was registered at Hillingdon, and the probate calendar places him at Hayes. The estate was 24,427 pounds.[^probate-reg-1977] A cause of death remembered in the family is not on the certificate we have, so it is not stated here. A studio portrait of a young man in a bow tie has no name on it, and it is not identified as Reg.

He was probably the boy of 12 on the same voyage to Cape Town in August 1916.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] He came back to London with his mother and Eileen on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, listed as Baron Fitzmaurice, a student, aged 19.[^passenger-1923-bendigo]

people.summary_de: Pats Vater. Baron ist sein Vorname, kein Titel. Er wurde am 21. August 1904 in der Ascension, Balham Hill, getauft, der Sohn von Edward Dixon und Edith Madeline Fitzmaurice. Er wurde wahrscheinlich am 26. Mai 1904 im Bezirk Wandsworth geboren. Wahrscheinlich heiratete er Lilian Maud Mary Bennett Ende 1927. Er starb am 31. März 1977.
people.story_de:
Reg war Baron Reginald FitzMaurice. Baron ist ein Vorname, kein Titel. Er wurde wahrscheinlich am 26. Mai 1904 im Bezirk Wandsworth geboren. Der Geburtsindex nennt seine Mutter als Spenser, eine Schreibweise von Spencer, Band 1d, Seite 670.[^gro-indexes] [^probate-reg-1977] Er wurde am 21. August 1904 in der Pfarrei the Ascension, Balham Hill, Eintrag 604, Seite 76, getauft. Das Register nennt ihn Baron Reginald, Sohn von Edward Dixon und Edith Madeline Fitzmaurice, aus 29 Cathles Road, und seinen Vater als Bauingenieur. Im Register steht kein Geburtsdatum.[^parish-ascension-balham-hill-1904-reg] 1911 ist er Baron Reginald, 6 Jahre alt, in der Schule, im Haushalt von Edward Dixon und Edith Madeline in Whitstable.[^census-1911-whitstable]

Wahrscheinlich heiratete er Lilian Maud Mary Bennett im Dezember-Quartal 1927 im Bezirk Hammersmith, Band 1a, Seite 661.[^gro-marriage-1927] Wählerverzeichnisse verorten ihn 1925 und 1926 in Wandsworth, von 1931 bis 1933 in Hammersmith, von 1934 bis 1937 im Bezirk Spelthorne und von 1938 bis etwa 1972 in Hayes.[^electoral-fitzmaurice] Am 11. Februar 1950 führte er seine Tochter Patricia in St Mary's, Wanstead, zum Altar. Das Album nennt ihn Mr R. Fitzmaurice of Hayes.[^album-1950]

Er starb am 31. März 1977. Der Tod wurde in Hillingdon registriert, und der Nachlasskalender verortet ihn in Hayes. Der Nachlass betrug 24.427 Pfund.[^probate-reg-1977] Eine in der Familie erinnerte Todesursache steht nicht auf der Urkunde, die wir haben, und wird deshalb hier nicht genannt. Ein Studioporträt eines jungen Mannes mit Fliege trägt keinen Namen, und es ist nicht als Reg identifiziert.

Wahrscheinlich war er der Junge von 12 Jahren auf derselben Reise nach Kapstadt im August 1916.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] Er kam mit seiner Mutter und Eileen auf der Bendigo nach London zurück, landete am 28. Dezember 1923 und ist als Baron Fitzmaurice geführt, Student, 19 Jahre alt.[^passenger-1923-bendigo]

people.summary: Pat's mother. Lilian Maud Mary Bennett, born about March 1900 at Bodmin, the youngest daughter of Charles Bennett and Annie, nee Grigg, who survived childhood. She probably died in the Uxbridge district in late 1947, aged 47.
people.story:
The wedding album's late Mrs R. Fitzmaurice was probably Lilian Maud Mary Bennett. She was born about March 1900 at Bodmin, Cornwall. The birth index, June quarter 1900, volume 5c, page 64, names her mother as Grigg, and the 1921 census gives the same three forenames, aged 21 years and 3 months, born at Bodmin.[^gro-lilian-death] [^census-1921-lilian] [^census-bennett]

Her parents were Charles Bennett, a tailor of Egloshayle and Bodmin, and Annie, probably Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg. Lilian was the youngest of the children who survived. In June 1921 she was a clerk at the Claims Record Office, boarding at Hampton Hill.[^census-1921-lilian] She probably married Baron Reginald FitzMaurice in the December quarter of 1927, in the Hammersmith district.[^gro-marriage-1927]

She probably died in the December quarter of 1947, in the Uxbridge district, which covered Hayes, aged 47.[^gro-lilian-death] The album of February 1950 therefore calls her the late Mrs R. Fitzmaurice.[^album-1950] No will and no grave have been found. A family memory that she died while Pat was a young child does not fit an age of about 18.

people.summary_de: Pats Mutter. Lilian Maud Mary Bennett, geboren etwa im März 1900 in Bodmin, die jüngste Tochter von Charles Bennett und Annie, geborene Grigg, die die Kindheit überlebte. Sie starb wahrscheinlich Ende 1947 im Bezirk Uxbridge, im Alter von 47 Jahren.
people.story_de:
Die verstorbene Mrs R. Fitzmaurice des Hochzeitsalbums war wahrscheinlich Lilian Maud Mary Bennett. Sie wurde etwa im März 1900 in Bodmin, Cornwall, geboren. Der Geburtsindex, Juni-Quartal 1900, Band 5c, Seite 64, nennt ihre Mutter als Grigg, und die Volkszählung von 1921 gibt dieselben drei Vornamen, 21 Jahre und 3 Monate alt, geboren in Bodmin.[^gro-lilian-death] [^census-1921-lilian] [^census-bennett]

Ihre Eltern waren Charles Bennett, ein Schneider aus Egloshayle und Bodmin, und Annie, wahrscheinlich Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg. Lilian war das jüngste der Kinder, die überlebten. Im Juni 1921 war sie Büroangestellte im Claims Record Office und wohnte zur Untermiete in Hampton Hill.[^census-1921-lilian] Wahrscheinlich heiratete sie Baron Reginald FitzMaurice im Dezember-Quartal 1927 im Bezirk Hammersmith.[^gro-marriage-1927]

Wahrscheinlich starb sie im Dezember-Quartal 1947 im Bezirk Uxbridge, zu dem Hayes gehörte, im Alter von 47 Jahren.[^gro-lilian-death] Das Album vom Februar 1950 nennt sie deshalb die verstorbene Mrs R. Fitzmaurice.[^album-1950] Weder ein Testament noch ein Grab wurde gefunden. Eine Familienerinnerung, sie sei gestorben, als Pat noch ein kleines Kind war, passt nicht zu einem Alter von etwa 18 Jahren.

people.summary: Reg's brother, called Bob. Edward Robert FitzMaurice, born in the Lambeth district in 1901. He married in Cape Town in 1925 and died at Port Elizabeth on 7 May 1981.
people.story:
The beach photograph is labelled Reg, Bob and their father Edward Dixon Fitzmaurice. Bob is Edward Robert Fitzmaurice, mother's maiden name Spencer, registered in the Lambeth district in the June quarter of 1901, volume 1d, page 503. In 1911 he was 9, at school, at Whitstable. He was probably the boy of 15 who sailed to Cape Town with his mother in August 1916.

On 30 October 1925, aged 24, a tramway engineer, he married Eileen Alice Yallop at St George's Cathedral, Cape Town. He was living at Auleta, Three Anchor Bay, and she at 7 Bertram Road, Sea Point. In 1926 their home was 17 Berkley Street, Gardens, when their son Edward Scott was baptised in the parish of Woodstock. Edward Scott died on 9 August 1935, aged 9, at Somerset Hospital. The home was then given as 1st Avenue, Bellville. Edward Robert died on 7 May 1981 at Port Elizabeth.

people.summary: Ron's father. Henry George Andrews, born at St Albans in April 1889, only child of Herbert Andrews and Lucy Stacey. He married Rosina Maud Cousins on 18 April 1915. He, Rosina and their son Sidney were killed at their home in Plaistow on 19 April 1941.
people.story:
Henry George Andrews was born at St Albans, Hertfordshire, in April 1889, and baptised at St Albans Abbey on 9 June 1889, son of Herbert and Lucy.[^parish-st-albans-1889] The birth index names his mother as Stacey.[^gro-indexes] He was their only child.[^census-andrews-stacey] In 1901 the family was at Hemel Hempstead. In 1911 he was a sawyer's labourer, living with his parents at Canning Town.

On 18 April 1915, aged 25, he married Rosina Maud Cousins at St Andrew's, Plaistow. His father is Herbert Andrews. Hers is William Cousins.[^parish-plaistow-1915] In 1921 he was a dock labourer for the Port of London Authority at the Royal Albert Docks, living at Plaistow in his father-in-law's house. In 1939 he was an explosive worker at the Royal filling factory, Woolwich.[^census-cousins] [^register-1939]

He was killed on 19 April 1941, aged 52, at the family home in Plaistow, in the West Ham county borough, together with Rosina and their son Sidney.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941] The wedding album's East Ham is the neighbouring borough. The Commonwealth War Graves record gives Plaistow.

people.story_de:
Henry George Andrews wurde im April 1889 in St Albans, Hertfordshire, geboren und am 9. Juni 1889 in der St Albans Abbey als Sohn von Herbert und Lucy getauft.[^parish-st-albans-1889] Der Geburtsindex nennt seine Mutter als Stacey.[^gro-indexes] Er war ihr einziges Kind.[^census-andrews-stacey] 1901 war die Familie in Hemel Hempstead. 1911 war er Hilfsarbeiter eines Sägers und lebte bei seinen Eltern in Canning Town.

Am 18. April 1915, 25 Jahre alt, heiratete er Rosina Maud Cousins in St Andrew's, Plaistow. Sein Vater ist Herbert Andrews. Ihrer ist William Cousins.[^parish-plaistow-1915] 1921 war er Dockarbeiter für die Port of London Authority in den Royal Albert Docks und lebte in Plaistow im Haus seines Schwiegervaters. 1939 war er Sprengstoffarbeiter in der Royal filling factory, Woolwich.[^census-cousins] [^register-1939]

Er wurde am 19. April 1941 im Alter von 52 Jahren im Familienhaus in Plaistow, im County Borough West Ham, zusammen mit Rosina und ihrem Sohn Sidney getötet.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941] Das East Ham des Hochzeitsalbums ist der benachbarte Bezirk. Der Eintrag der Commonwealth War Graves nennt Plaistow.

people.summary: Ron's mother. Rosina Maud Cousins, born at Bermondsey on 14 November 1881, daughter of William Cousins and Annie, nee Gall. She married Henry George Andrews on 18 April 1915 and was killed with him at Plaistow on 19 April 1941.
people.story:
Rosina Maud Cousins was born on 14 November 1881 at Bermondsey, and registered in the St Olave district, volume 1d, page 292. Her mother's maiden name was Gall.[^gro-cousins-gall] She was one of eight children of William Cousins, a dock labourer born at Hackney, and Annie, nee Gall, born at Thetford.[^census-cousins]

On 18 April 1915 she married Henry George Andrews at St Andrew's, Plaistow.[^parish-plaistow-1915] Their children were Herbert William, Ronald and Sidney George. The home in Plaistow had been her father's. She, Henry and Sidney were killed there on 19 April 1941. Rosina was 59.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941]

Am 18. April 1915 heiratete sie Henry George Andrews in St Andrew's, Plaistow.[^parish-plaistow-1915] Ihre Kinder waren Herbert William, Ronald und Sidney George. people.summary: Ron's elder brother. Herbert William Andrews, born in the West Ham district in 1916. Probably married Christina M. Knight in 1940. Father of Christine Ellis. His death has not been found.
people.story:
Herbert William Andrews, mother's maiden name Cousins, was registered in the West Ham district in the September quarter of 1916, volume 4a, page 180.[^gro-indexes] In 1921 he was 4, a grandson in the household of his maternal grandfather William Cousins at 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow, with his parents Henry George and Rosina Maud Andrews. In 1939 he was single and an explosive worker at the Royal filling factory, Woolwich, in the same household as his father.[^census-cousins] [^register-1939] The exact day on that register is not published here, because his death has not been found.

He was probably the Herbert W. Andrews who married Christina M. Knight in the September quarter of 1940, in the East Ham district, volume 4a, page 561.[^gro-indexes] Their daughter is Christine Ellis. He was at Pat and Ron's wedding in 1950, named as Herb.[^album-1950] A family memory that he has died has no date on a record yet, so no death is stated.

people.story_de:
Herbert William Andrews, Mädchenname der Mutter Cousins, wurde im Bezirk West Ham im September-Quartal 1916 registriert, Band 4a, Seite 180.[^gro-indexes] 1921 war er 4, ein Enkel im Haushalt seines Großvaters mütterlicherseits William Cousins in 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow, mit seinen Eltern Henry George und Rosina Maud Andrews. 1939 war er ledig und Sprengstoffarbeiter in der Royal filling factory, Woolwich, im selben Haushalt wie sein Vater.[^census-cousins] [^register-1939] Der genaue Tag in diesem Register wird hier nicht veröffentlicht, weil sein Tod nicht gefunden wurde.

Wahrscheinlich war er der Herbert W. Andrews, der Christina M. Knight im September-Quartal 1940 im Bezirk East Ham heiratete, Band 4a, Seite 561.[^gro-indexes] Ihre Tochter ist Christine Ellis. Er war 1950 bei der Hochzeit von Pat und Ron, genannt als Herb.[^album-1950] Eine Familienerinnerung, dass er gestorben sei, hat noch kein Datum in einer Quelle, daher wird kein Tod angegeben.

The war-dead record names him as the son of Henry George and Rosina Maud Andrews.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941]

people.summary: Son of Henry George Andrews and Rosina Maud Cousins. Probably born in the summer of 1921 in the West Ham district. He married Patricia Mary FitzMaurice on 11 February 1950. Leading Aircraftman with No. 111 Maintenance Unit at Tura, and art editor of the Tura Times in 1945. He died in 2010 (family). Father of Amanda and Venetia.
people.story:
Ronald Andrews was probably born in the summer of 1921 in the West Ham district, son of Henry George Andrews and Rosina Maud Cousins, and brother of Herbert William and Sidney George.[^family-testimony] He married Patricia Mary FitzMaurice at St Mary's, Wanstead, on 11 February 1950.[^album-1950] He is the father of Amanda and Venetia.

His wartime photograph album has its own page. The press card names him Leading Aircraftman R. Andrews, art editor of the Tura Times, the newspaper of No. 111 Maintenance Unit, in 1945.[^ron-album] He died in 2010 (family).[^family-testimony] Pat died in 2020 (family). Pat and Ron are buried together in the churchyard of St John the Baptist Parish Church, Waterloo Road, Crowthorne, Berkshire (family).[^st-john-crowthorne-churchyard] No home address is published.

media.transcription:
[Typed press card]
PRESS CARD.
This is to certify that the undermentioned airman is Art Editor of the "Tura Times", Unit newspaper of 111 M.U. R.A.F. It is requested that all possible help be given him in this connection.
L.A.C. R. ANDREWS.
[signature] Editor.
[signature] G/Capt. Commanding Officer.

[Handwritten]
About this time I was roped in this-wise

[Newspaper]
Tura Times ... PEACE AFTER NEARLY SIX YEARS ... V.J. ... FIRST PEACE EDITION
In colour this looked all right.

[Under a drawing]
Photo of a drawing of a photo ... Betty Hutton

[Under two portraits]
No ... comment!

Dashes in the original are shown here as '...'.

media.caption: Ron's album: Tutankhamun's mask and coffin, and the note that the treasures were "stored in our caves"
media.alt: Album page with photographs of the gold mask of Tutankhamun, the Egyptian Museum entrance and the gold coffin, above a handwritten note
media.transcription:
Mummy-mask of beaten gold of King Tutankhamen
Entrance to Egyptian Museum Cairo
Outer mummy-case of solid gold of Tutankhamen

The two end pictures here shew two items in the fabulous collection of ancient relics found in the sealed tomb of the young King Tutankhamen. The twin chambers of the tomb lay undisturbed for 5000 years and when opened, their hoard of priceless treasures took ten years to catalogue and transport up the Nile to this Museum. The treasures were stored in our caves during the War and later placed on view in the Museum. They were worth the journey to see.

Ronald Andrews wurde wahrscheinlich im Sommer 1921 im Bezirk West Ham geboren, als Sohn von Henry George Andrews und Rosina Maud Cousins und als Bruder von Herbert William und Sidney George.[^family-testimony] Er heiratete Patricia Mary FitzMaurice am 11. Februar 1950 in St Mary's, Wanstead.[^album-1950] Er ist der Vater von Amanda und Venetia.

Sein Fotoalbum aus der Kriegszeit hat eine eigene Seite. Der Presseausweis nennt ihn Leading Aircraftman R. Andrews, Grafikredakteur der Tura Times, der Zeitung der No. 111 Maintenance Unit, im Jahr 1945.[^ron-album] Er starb 2010 (Familie).[^family-testimony] Pat starb 2020 (Familie). Pat und Ron sind gemeinsam auf dem Kirchhof der St John the Baptist Parish Church, Waterloo Road, Crowthorne, Berkshire, beigesetzt (Familie).[^st-john-crowthorne-churchyard] Es wird keine Wohnadresse veröffentlicht.

people.summary: Patricia Mary FitzMaurice, daughter of Baron Reginald FitzMaurice and Lilian Maud Mary Bennett. Probably born in the Hammersmith district in early 1929. The family remembers Windsor, which is not the registered birthplace. She married Ronald Andrews on 11 February 1950. Pat died in 2020 (family). Pat and Ron are buried together in the churchyard of St John the Baptist Parish Church, Waterloo Road, Crowthorne, Berkshire (family). Mother of Amanda and Venetia.
people.story:
Patricia Mary Andrews, nee FitzMaurice, was the daughter of Baron Reginald FitzMaurice and Lilian Maud Mary Bennett. She was probably born in the Hammersmith district in early 1929. The family remembers Windsor. That memory is not the registered birthplace.[^family-testimony] She married Ronald Andrews at St Mary's, Wanstead, on 11 February 1950.[^album-1950] She is the mother of Amanda and Venetia.

Pat died in 2020 (family). Pat and Ron are buried together in the churchyard of St John the Baptist Parish Church, Waterloo Road, Crowthorne, Berkshire (family).[^family-testimony] [^st-john-crowthorne-churchyard] Among her papers were two Evening News cuttings about Cecil FitzMaurice, later Earl of Orkney. No home address is published.

media.caption: Wedding album, title pages: "Ronald and Patricia" and the dedication naming both sets of parents
media.alt: The open wedding album: a label reading Ronald and Patricia, and a handwritten page naming the couple, their parents, the church and the date
media.transcription:
[Label on the left page]
Ronald and Patricia

[Right page, under the monogram RP]
A pictorial record of the Wedding of Patricia Mary, daughter of Mr. and the late Mrs. R. Fitzmaurice, of Hayes, Middlesex, to Ronald, son of the late Mr. and Mrs. H. G. Andrews, of East Ham, London. The Marriage was solemnized by the Reverend A. E. [or A. C.] Gates, at St. Mary's Church, Wanstead, at 10.30 a.m., on Saturday, February 11th., 1950.

media.caption: Wedding album: the first photograph, the couple walking down the aisle

nameVariants.name: "Fiery Face"
nameVariants.note: from a red birthmark on his face

people.summary: King of Scots from the age of six, after the murder of his father in 1437. He was killed when one of his own cannon exploded at the siege of Roxburgh in 1460.
people.story:
James II became King of Scots in 1437, at the age of six, after his father James I was murdered. He was known as "Fiery Face" for a red birthmark on one side of his face.[^wiki-james-ii]

He married Mary of Guelders in 1449. In August 1460 he was besieging Roxburgh Castle, then held by the English, when one of his cannon exploded beside him and killed him. He was 29.[^wiki-james-ii]

His daughter Mary Stewart married into the Hamilton family, and through her the Hamiltons came close to the Scottish throne.[^wiki-mary-stewart]

## Link to this family

Earlier versions of this site traced Sebastian's line to this person through Edward Dixon FitzMaurice. That link is not proven, and the 1890 London Gazette record speaks against it (see Edward Dixon FitzMaurice). This person is shown in a separate frame for that reason.[^gazette-1890][^site-earlier]

people.summary_de: König der Schotten vom sechsten Lebensjahr an, nach der Ermordung seines Vaters 1437. Er wurde getötet, als 1460 bei der Belagerung von Roxburgh eine seiner eigenen Kanonen explodierte.
people.story_de:
James II wurde 1437 im Alter von sechs Jahren König der Schotten, nachdem sein Vater James I ermordet worden war. Er war wegen eines roten Muttermals auf einer Seite seines Gesichts als "Fiery Face" (Feuergesicht) bekannt.[^wiki-james-ii]

Er heiratete Mary of Guelders 1449. Im August 1460 belagerte er Roxburgh Castle, das damals von den Engländern gehalten wurde, als eine seiner Kanonen neben ihm explodierte und ihn tötete. Er war 29.[^wiki-james-ii]

Seine Tochter Mary Stewart heiratete in die Familie Hamilton ein, und durch sie kamen die Hamiltons dem schottischen Thron nahe.[^wiki-mary-stewart]

people.summary: Daughter of James II. After a first marriage to Thomas Boyd was annulled, she married James, 1st Lord Hamilton, in 1474. Her son became the first Hamilton Earl of Arran.
people.story:
Mary Stewart was the elder daughter of King James II and Mary of Guelders. By 1467 she had been married to Thomas Boyd, who was made Earl of Arran. His family fell from power and the marriage was annulled.[^wiki-mary-stewart]

In 1474 she married James, 1st Lord Hamilton, who was almost forty years older than her. A papal dispensation for the marriage followed in 1476.[^wiki-mary-stewart] Their son James became the 1st Earl of Arran.[^wiki-arran-1][^aah-hamilton] Earlier pages called that son her grandson, which is wrong, and gave her dates as about 1433 to 1465, which are also wrong.[^site-earlier]

No portrait of her is known. The portrait shown with her father is of her mother, Mary of Guelders.[^site-earlier]

James Hamilton, 1st Lord Hamilton, married Mary Stewart, daughter of King James II, in 1474. He was almost forty years older than his bride.[^wiki-mary-stewart] He died in 1479. Their son James became the 1st Earl of Arran.[^wiki-arran-1]

The Hamilton family seat was later Hamilton Palace in Lanarkshire, which earlier pages show with him.[^site-earlier]

people.summary: Son of Mary Stewart and Lord Hamilton, made Earl of Arran. Earlier pages called him Mary's grandson and said he was Regent; both are wrong.
people.story:
James Hamilton was the son of Mary Stewart and James, 1st Lord Hamilton, and so a grandson of King James II. He was made Earl of Arran.[^wiki-arran-1][^aah-hamilton]

He married first Elizabeth Home, in about 1490, and then Janet Bethune in 1516. His son by Janet became the 2nd Earl of Arran and Duke of Châtellerault.[^wiki-arran-1][^wiki-chatellerault]

Earlier pages called him Mary's grandson and said he was Regent of Scotland. He was her son, and it was his son, not he, who became Regent.[^site-earlier][^wiki-chatellerault]

James Hamilton war der Sohn von Mary Stewart und James, 1. Lord Hamilton, und damit ein Enkel von König James II. Er wurde zum Earl of Arran erhoben.[^wiki-arran-1][^aah-hamilton]

Er heiratete zuerst Elizabeth Home, etwa 1490, und dann 1516 Janet Bethune. Sein Sohn mit Janet wurde der 2. Earl of Arran und Duke of Châtellerault.[^wiki-arran-1][^wiki-chatellerault]

Frühere Seiten nannten ihn Marys Enkel und sagten, er sei Regent von Schottland gewesen. Er war ihr Sohn, und sein Sohn, nicht er, wurde Regent.[^site-earlier][^wiki-chatellerault]

people.summary: Regent of Scotland for the young Mary, Queen of Scots, from 1543 to 1554, and made Duke of Châtellerault in France in 1549.
people.story:
James Hamilton, 2nd Earl of Arran, was the son of the 1st Earl and Janet Bethune. As the nearest adult heir to the throne, he governed Scotland as Regent for the infant Mary, Queen of Scots, from 1543 to 1554.[^wiki-chatellerault]

In February 1549 the French king made him Duke of Châtellerault. He died in January 1575. His third son John became the 1st Marquess of Hamilton.[^wiki-chatellerault][^wiki-marquess-1]

people.story:

Earlier pages say he was executed for that loyalty in 1649.[^site-earlier]

His daughter Anne later inherited the dukedom in her own right.[^wiki-anne-duchess]

people.summary: Daughter of the 1st Duke, Duchess of Hamilton in her own right. She married William Douglas in 1656, and their son George became the 1st Earl of Orkney.
people.story:
Anne Hamilton was the daughter of the 1st Duke of Hamilton and inherited the dukedom in her own right.[^wiki-anne-duchess][^nts-anne] On 29 April 1656 she married William Douglas, Earl of Selkirk, who was made Duke of Hamilton for life in 1660.[^wiki-anne-duchess][^wiki-william-duke]

Their sons included Lord George Hamilton, who became the 1st Earl of Orkney.[^wiki-george-orkney] The family crest page dates her marriage to 1643; the correct year is 1656.[^site-earlier][^wiki-anne-duchess] She died in October 1716, aged 84.[^wiki-anne-duchess]

people.summary: A son of Anne, Duchess of Hamilton. A career soldier, he was made Earl of Orkney in 1696 and in 1736 became the first Field Marshal in the British Army.
people.story:
Lord George Hamilton was a son of Anne, Duchess of Hamilton, and William Douglas, and was baptised in February 1666.[^wiki-george-orkney] He was a soldier for most of his life and served under the Duke of Marlborough; earlier pages show him with the Battle of Blenheim of 1704.[^wiki-george-orkney][^site-earlier]

On 25 November 1695 he married Elizabeth Villiers, and on 3 January 1696 he was made Earl of Orkney.[^wiki-george-orkney] He bought Cliveden in Buckinghamshire and lived there and at Taplow.[^wiki-george-orkney] He was appointed Governor of Virginia but never went there. In 1736 he became the first officer in the British Army to hold the rank of Field Marshal, and he died in January 1737.[^wiki-george-orkney]

He had daughters but no son. The earldom could pass to a daughter, and his eldest, Anne, became the 2nd Countess.[^wiki-george-orkney][^wiki-anne-countess]

people.summary_de: Ein Sohn von Anne, Duchess of Hamilton. Als Berufssoldat wurde er 1696 zum Earl of Orkney erhoben und wurde 1736 der erste Feldmarschall in der British Army.
people.story_de:
Lord George Hamilton war ein Sohn von Anne, Duchess of Hamilton, und William Douglas und wurde im Februar 1666 getauft.[^wiki-george-orkney] Er war den größten Teil seines Lebens Soldat und diente unter dem Duke of Marlborough; frühere Seiten zeigen ihn mit der Schlacht bei Blenheim von 1704.[^wiki-george-orkney][^site-earlier]

Am 25. November 1695 heiratete er Elizabeth Villiers, und am 3. Januar 1696 wurde er zum Earl of Orkney erhoben.[^wiki-george-orkney] Er kaufte Cliveden in Buckinghamshire und lebte dort und in Taplow.[^wiki-george-orkney] Er wurde zum Gouverneur von Virginia ernannt, reiste aber nie dorthin. 1736 wurde er der erste Offizier der British Army, der den Rang eines Feldmarschalls innehatte, und er starb im Januar 1737.[^wiki-george-orkney]

Er hatte Töchter, aber keinen Sohn. Das Earldom konnte an eine Tochter übergehen, und seine älteste, Anne, wurde die 2. Countess.[^wiki-george-orkney][^wiki-anne-countess]

She died on 10 May 1791, though some accounts give 1790. Her daughter Mary succeeded her.[^wiki-mary-3rd][^wiki-kirkwall]

people.summary: Born John FitzMaurice, he took the name Petty and became Earl of Shelburne. His sons were the future Prime Minister, Lord Shelburne, and Thomas FitzMaurice.
people.story:
John Petty was born John FitzMaurice in 1706, a younger son of the Earl of Kerry. He took the surname Petty on inheriting the estates of his uncle, and was made Earl of Shelburne. He died in May 1761.[^wiki-shelburne-1]

His elder son William became Prime Minister and Marquess of Lansdowne. His younger son Thomas kept the name FitzMaurice and married Mary O'Brien, later 4th Countess of Orkney, which is how the Earls of Orkney came to be FitzMaurices.[^wiki-shelburne-1][^wiki-thomas-mp][^wiki-mary-4th]

He died in November 1820, eleven years before his mother, so he never became Earl. people.story:
Thomas FitzMaurice was the son of John, Viscount Kirkwall, and Anna Maria Blaquiere. He succeeded his grandmother as 5th Earl of Orkney in 1831.[^wiki-5th-earl] He sat in the House of Lords as a Scottish representative peer from 1833 to 1874.[^wiki-5th-earl]

In 1826 he married Charlotte Irby. Among their eight children were George, later the 6th Earl, Henry Warrender FitzMaurice and Frederick O'Bryen FitzMaurice.[^wiki-5th-earl][^peerage-henry-warrender][^peerage-frederick] He died in May 1877.[^wiki-5th-earl]

The family crest page says he became Earl in 1826, which was the year of his marriage, and an earlier page ends his time as a representative peer in 1871.[^site-earlier]

Henry Warrender FitzMaurice was a younger son of the 5th Earl of Orkney. He married Sarah Jane Roose on 5 September 1861 and died in January 1875, two years before his father.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-5th-earl]

The peerage records list four children: Henry George Hamilton (1863 to 1888), Edmond Walter (1867 to 1951), Isabella Emily (about 1868 to 1928) and Alexander (1874 to 1922).[^peerage-henry-warrender] In 1890, after Edmond became the 7th Earl, a royal warrant gave the rank of an earl's children to his surviving brother and sister, Alexander Edmond and Isabella Emily.[^gazette-1890]

Earlier versions of this site said Henry Warrender was almost certainly the father of Edward Dixon FitzMaurice. He does not appear in any of these records, so that link is not shown.[^site-earlier][^gazette-1890]

people.summary: Son of Henry Warrender. He succeeded his uncle as Earl in 1889, aged 22, and in 1892 married the Gaiety star Connie Gilchrist. Their only child died before him, and the title passed to a distant cousin.
people.story:
Edmond Walter FitzMaurice was the son of Henry Warrender FitzMaurice and Sarah Jane Roose. He succeeded his uncle George as 7th Earl of Orkney in October 1889, aged 22.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-6th-earl] In April 1890 a royal warrant gave his surviving brother and sister the rank of an earl's children; it names no other siblings.[^gazette-1890]

On 19 July 1892 he married Connie Gilchrist, a former child performer of the Gaiety Theatre.[^wiki-connie] The Evening News of 1951 describes him as of The Tythe House, Stewkley, near Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds.[^korea-clipping]

Their only child, Lady Mary Constance Hamilton FitzMaurice, was born in 1903. She married, had no children, and died in October 1950, ten months before her father.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-connie] When Edmond died in August 1951 he left the residue of his estate of £42,893 to Cecil FitzMaurice, who also inherited the earldom. The paper called Edmond Cecil's great-uncle; by the peerage records he was Cecil's first cousin twice removed.[^korea-clipping][^press-1951][^peerage-cecil]

Earlier pages give his name as "Edmond Walter Leighton FitzMaurice" and say he inherited at 16. "Leighton" comes from the Leighton Buzzard address, and he was 22.[^site-earlier][^korea-clipping]

media.transcription:
EARL FROM KOREA LEFT A FORTUNE
HE SCRUBBED DECKS
[handwritten: 1951]
"Evening News" Reporter
THIRTY-TWO-YEAR-OLD Cecil O'Bryen Fitzmaurice, who became the Eighth Earl of Orkney while serving as an R.A.S.C. driver in Korea, has been left the residue of a £42,893 estate by his great-uncle, the Seventh Earl, it is revealed to-day.
The Rt. Hon. Edmond Walter Fitzmaurice, Seventh Earl of Orkney, of The Tythe House, Stewkley, Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds, died last August, aged 84.

Late Back Aboard
The seventh Earl was married for 54 years to Miss Connie Gilchrist, the Gaiety star of the 'nineties who died in 1946, aged 73.
The new Earl, known to his friends as "Ginger" in the Army, arrived home by troopship last October.
On the way home the ship called at Colombo. For arriving back late he received four days C.B. and scrubbed mess-decks.
He is now living with his mother, Mrs. Dorothy Wiggins, at Lantern Hatch, Itchingfield, near Horsham, Sussex.

Juli 1892 heiratete er Connie Gilchrist, eine frühere Kinderdarstellerin des Gaiety Theatre.[^wiki-connie] Der Evening News von 1951 beschreibt ihn als aus The Tythe House, Stewkley, near Leighton Buzzard, als Deputy Lieutenant für Buckinghamshire und als früheren Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds.[^korea-clipping]

Ihr einziges Kind, Lady Mary Constance Hamilton FitzMaurice, wurde 1903 geboren. Sie heiratete, hatte keine Kinder und starb im Oktober 1950, zehn Monate vor ihrem Vater.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-connie] Als Edmond im August 1951 starb, hinterließ er Cecil FitzMaurice den Rest seines Nachlasses von £42,893; Cecil erbte auch das Earldom. Die Zeitung nannte Edmond Cecils Großonkel; nach den Peerage-Belegen war er Cecils Cousin ersten Grades mit zwei Generationen Abstand.[^korea-clipping][^press-1951][^peerage-cecil]

Frühere Seiten geben seinen Namen als "Edmond Walter Leighton FitzMaurice" an und sagen, er habe mit 16 geerbt. "Leighton" stammt von der Adresse in Leighton Buzzard, und er war 22.[^site-earlier][^korea-clipping]

people.summary: Child model for Whistler and Leighton and a star of the Gaiety Theatre, she married Edmond, 7th Earl of Orkney, in 1892.
people.story:
Connie Gilchrist was born in January 1865. As a child she modelled for painters: Whistler painted her as "The Gold Girl", posed as she appeared on the Gaiety Theatre stage in her skipping-rope dance, and she was the girl in Frederic Leighton's "The Music Lesson".[^wiki-connie][^met-gold-girl] She performed at the Gaiety and became known as "the original Gaiety Girl".[^wiki-connie]

She had left the stage by July 1892, when she married Edmond FitzMaurice, 7th Earl of Orkney.[^wiki-connie] They were married for 54 years. She died in May 1946.[^wiki-connie][^korea-clipping] The 1951 newspaper report gives her age at death as 73; from her date of birth she was 81.[^korea-clipping][^wiki-connie]

people.story:
Lady Mary Constance Hamilton FitzMaurice was the only child of Edmond, 7th Earl of Orkney, and Connie Gilchrist. She was born in February 1903.[^peerage-henry-warrender] She married and became Lady Mary Gosling, but had no children.[^wiki-connie]

She died on 6 October 1950, ten months before her father. The earldom could pass to a daughter, so had she outlived him she would probably have inherited it.[^wiki-earl-of-orkney] Instead it went to Cecil FitzMaurice, a distant cousin.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^peerage-cecil]

people.summary: A distant cousin of the 7th Earl, he inherited the earldom in 1951 while serving as an Army driver in Korea. He married Rose Silley at Brixham in 1953.
people.story:
Cecil O'Bryen FitzMaurice was the younger son of Douglas Frederick Harold FitzMaurice and Dorothy Dickie. He joined the Royal Army Service Corps in 1939 and served in North Africa, Italy, France and Germany, and then in Korea.[^wiki-cecil][^peerage-cecil]

He became the 8th Earl of Orkney on 21 August 1951 while serving as a driver in Korea. Newspapers called him "the Earl from Korea".[^press-1951][^korea-clipping] The Evening News reported that his Army friends knew him as "Ginger", that the 7th Earl had left him the residue of an estate of £42,893, and that on the voyage home he was given four days' confinement to barracks and set to scrub the mess decks for coming back late to the ship at Colombo.[^korea-clipping] The paper called the 7th Earl his great-uncle; he was in fact a much more distant cousin.[^korea-clipping][^peerage-cecil]

On 27 November 1953 he married Rose Katherine Durk Silley at St Mary's, Brixham. The Evening News said she helped her mother run a 60-bedroom hotel in the town, and that the Earl had once worked in a garage.[^marries-clipping][^peerage-cecil] Rose died in 1995. Cecil died in February 1998 with no children, and the earldom passed to a distant cousin, Peter St John.[^wiki-cecil][^wiki-earl-of-orkney]

Earlier pages give the year of his marriage as 1952. The peerage records give 1953.[^site-earlier][^peerage-cecil]

media.caption: Evening News, 1951: "Earl from Korea left a fortune. He scrubbed decks"
media.alt: A narrow newspaper cutting with the headline Earl from Korea Left a Fortune, He Scrubbed Decks
media.transcription:
EARL FROM KOREA LEFT A FORTUNE
HE SCRUBBED DECKS
[handwritten: 1951]
"Evening News" Reporter
THIRTY-TWO-YEAR-OLD Cecil O'Bryen Fitzmaurice, who became the Eighth Earl of Orkney while serving as an R.A.S.C. driver in Korea, has been left the residue of a £42,893 estate by his great-uncle, the Seventh Earl, it is revealed to-day.
The Rt. Hon. Edmond Walter Fitzmaurice, Seventh Earl of Orkney, of The Tythe House, Stewkley, Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds, died last August, aged 84.

Late Back Aboard
The seventh Earl was married for 54 years to Miss Connie Gilchrist, the Gaiety star of the 'nineties who died in 1946, aged 73.
The new Earl, known to his friends as "Ginger" in the Army, arrived home by troopship last October.
On the way home the ship called at Colombo. For arriving back late he received four days C.B. and scrubbed mess-decks.
He is now living with his mother, Mrs. Dorothy Wiggins, at Lantern Hatch, Itchingfield, near Horsham, Sussex.

EARL OF ORKNEY MARRIES
"Evening News" Woman Reporter
MISS ROSE SILLEY, aged 34, who helps her mother run a 60-bedroomed hotel at Brixham, Devon, was married at St. Mary's, Brixham, to-day to the 34-year-old Earl of Orkney. Their engagement was announced on Tuesday.
The Earl, who is the eighth earl, succeeded to the title in 1951 when he was a driver with the R.A.S.C. in Korea, at one time worked in a garage.

occupations.note_de: Im Royal Kalendar von 1827 bis 1841 aufgeführt; in der Liste von 1842 nicht mehr enthalten. Wahrscheinlich dieser John (C0731). people.cardPlace: Tower of London, Mile End, and Tower Hill
people.summary: Clerk in the Board of Ordnance at the Tower of London, listed as a Junior Clerk under the Surveyor General from 1827 to 1841. The 1841 page was read from the image. He married Eliza Taylor at St Martin's, Birmingham, on 3 February 1827. Father of William, John Richard and Robert William. He was probably of Holmes Street, Commercial Road, in 1830, and of Old Mint, Tower Hill, in 1834. By 1861 he was described as a gentleman. His birth, parents and death have not been found.
people.story: John FitzMaurice married Eliza Taylor by licence at St Martin's, Birmingham, on 3 February 1827. The register describes him as of His Majesty's Tower of London, a bachelor, and Eliza as of that parish, a spinster. John Taylor witnessed the marriage.[^parish-birmingham-1827] He was a clerk with the Board of Ordnance: a clerk at their son William's baptism in 1827, a clerk in the Ordnance Office in 1829, and a clerk in the Tower in 1832.[^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] [^parish-stepney-1832] The family lived in Whitechapel and then in Mile End Old Town. By 1861, when Robert William married, the register calls John a gentleman.[^parish-battersea-1861] In 1871 his son John Richard gave his own birthplace as the Tower of London.[^census-1871-edgbaston-jrf] The Royal Kalendar for 1827 lists a John Fitzmaurice as a Junior Clerk under the Surveyor General of the Board of Ordnance. The same name stays in that list through the 1841 volume and is gone from 1842.[^royal-kalendar-1827-ordnance] [^royal-kalendar-1828-1841-ordnance] [^royal-kalendar-1842-1845-ordnance] The 1841 volume, printed page 212, was read from the page image: he stands between Hy. King and Anty. Harvey.[^royal-kalendar-1841-ordnance-page] That is probably this John: the parish registers already call him a clerk in the Ordnance Office and in the Tower at the same dates. The lists do not give his age, birthplace or parents. The GRO death index on FreeBMD has no John Fitzmaurice in 1841 or 1842. A John Fitzmaurice death was registered in the December quarter of 1840 at Bloomsbury, volume 1, page 74. That entry is almost certainly an infant: John Fitzmaurice, aged one and a half, was buried at St Giles in the Fields on 15 December 1840. St Giles was in the Bloomsbury registration district. That death is not this John.[^freebmd-john-fitzmaurice-deaths-1840-1842] [^parish-st-giles-1840-john-fitzmaurice-burial] Sun Fire Office catalogue entries name a John Fitzmaurice, gentleman, of 33 Holmes Street, Charles Street, Commercial Road, on 25 November 1830, and of 27 Old Mint, opposite the Irish Barracks, Tower Hill, on 21 January 1834. The original policy books have not been seen. Those addresses fit this John, and the identification is probable rather than proved. Holmes Street was renamed Exmouth Street in 1867 and has since gone. The Irish Barracks stood in the old Mint area inside the Tower, so the 1834 house was probably within the Tower walls, a few steps from the Ordnance offices.[^underground-map-exmouth-street] [^he-irish-barracks-tower][^sun-fire-1830-john-fitzmaurice-holmes-street] [^sun-fire-1834-john-fitzmaurice-old-mint] John's own birth, his parents and his death have not been found. He has not been found with Eliza in the 1841 or 1851 census. A published family history places him in a Carlow branch of the FitzMaurices of Kerry. The London entries in that account now agree with these registers. No record found so far states where he was born or who his parents were, so that origin stays likely but not proved.[^fitzmaurice-family-carlow]

openQuestions.question: Where was he born, and who were his parents?
openQuestions.record: A record that names his father: the September quarter 1840 St Martin in the Fields marriage of a John Fitzmaurice, if it is his, or a Carlow family register. See the research notes page.

openQuestions.question: When did he and Eliza die?
openQuestions.record: Possible deaths are listed as leads on the research notes page: Eliza, 1839 or 1845; John, Brentford, 1865.

openQuestions.question: When and why did he leave the Ordnance between the 1841 and 1842 Royal Kalendars?
openQuestions.record: A death, retirement or transfer in 1841 or early 1842 would fit. The December 1840 Bloomsbury death is an infant buried at St Giles in the Fields, not this clerk, so his death is open again. The FreeBMD index has no John Fitzmaurice death in 1841 or 1842; later London deaths in 1848 and 1860 are leads. A John Fitzmoriss, 32, born Middlesex, is indexed at St John Wapping in the 1841 census and still has to be read. See the research notes page.

people.summary_de: Schreiber im Board of Ordnance im Tower of London, von 1827 bis 1841 als Juniorschreiber unter dem Surveyor General aufgeführt. Die Seite von 1841 wurde anhand des Bildes gelesen. Er heiratete Eliza Taylor am 3. Februar 1827 in St Martin's, Birmingham. Vater von William, John Richard und Robert William. Er war wahrscheinlich 1830 aus Holmes Street, Commercial Road, und 1834 aus Old Mint, Tower Hill. 1861 wurde er als Gentleman bezeichnet. Seine Geburt, seine Eltern und sein Tod sind nicht gefunden worden.
people.story_de: John FitzMaurice heiratete Eliza Taylor am 3. Februar 1827 mit Lizenz in St Martin's, Birmingham. Das Register bezeichnet ihn als aus His Majesty's Tower of London und als Junggesellen, Eliza als aus dieser Gemeinde und als ledig. John Taylor bezeugte die Heirat.[^parish-birmingham-1827] Er war Schreiber beim Board of Ordnance: Schreiber bei der Taufe ihres Sohnes William 1827, Schreiber im Ordnance Office 1829 und Schreiber im Tower 1832.[^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] [^parish-stepney-1832] Die Familie lebte in Whitechapel und danach in Mile End Old Town. 1861, als Robert William heiratete, nennt das Register John einen Gentleman.[^parish-battersea-1861] 1871 gab sein Sohn John Richard als eigenen Geburtsort den Tower of London an.[^census-1871-edgbaston-jrf] Der Royal Kalendar für 1827 führt einen John Fitzmaurice als Juniorschreiber unter dem Surveyor General des Board of Ordnance auf. Derselbe Name bleibt in dieser Liste bis zum Band von 1841 und fehlt ab 1842.[^royal-kalendar-1827-ordnance] [^royal-kalendar-1828-1841-ordnance] [^royal-kalendar-1842-1845-ordnance] Der Band von 1841, gedruckte Seite 212, wurde anhand des Seitenbildes gelesen: er steht zwischen Hy. King und Anty. Harvey.[^royal-kalendar-1841-ordnance-page] Das ist wahrscheinlich dieser John: die Kirchenregister nennen ihn zu denselben Zeitpunkten bereits Schreiber im Ordnance Office und im Tower. Die Listen geben sein Alter, seinen Geburtsort und seine Eltern nicht an. Der GRO-Sterbeindex bei FreeBMD enthält keinen John Fitzmaurice für 1841 oder 1842. Ein Sterbefall John Fitzmaurice wurde im Dezemberquartal 1840 in Bloomsbury eingetragen, Band 1, Seite 74. Dieser Eintrag betrifft mit ziemlicher Sicherheit ein Kleinkind: John Fitzmaurice, eineinhalb Jahre alt, wurde am 15. Dezember 1840 in St Giles in the Fields begraben. St Giles lag im Registrierungsbezirk Bloomsbury. Dieser Sterbefall ist nicht dieser John.[^freebmd-john-fitzmaurice-deaths-1840-1842] [^parish-st-giles-1840-john-fitzmaurice-burial] Katalogeinträge des Sun Fire Office nennen einen John Fitzmaurice, Gentleman, aus 33 Holmes Street, Charles Street, Commercial Road, am 25. November 1830, und aus 27 Old Mint, opposite the Irish Barracks, Tower Hill, am 21. Januar 1834. Die ursprünglichen Policenbücher sind nicht eingesehen worden. Diese Adressen passen zu diesem John, und die Zuordnung ist wahrscheinlich, nicht bewiesen. Holmes Street wurde 1867 in Exmouth Street umbenannt und besteht seither nicht mehr. Die Irish Barracks standen im Bereich des Old Mint innerhalb des Tower, sodass das Haus von 1834 wahrscheinlich innerhalb der Mauern des Tower lag, wenige Schritte von den Ordnance offices entfernt.[^underground-map-exmouth-street] [^he-irish-barracks-tower][^sun-fire-1830-john-fitzmaurice-holmes-street] [^sun-fire-1834-john-fitzmaurice-old-mint] Johns eigene Geburt, seine Eltern und sein Tod sind nicht gefunden worden. Er ist mit Eliza weder in der Volkszählung von 1841 noch in der von 1851 gefunden worden. Eine veröffentlichte Familiengeschichte stellt ihn in einen Zweig der FitzMaurices of Kerry in Carlow. Die Einträge zu London in dieser Darstellung stimmen nun mit diesen Registern überein. Kein bisher gefundener Beleg nennt, wo er geboren wurde oder wer seine Eltern waren, sodass diese Herkunft wahrscheinlich bleibt, aber nicht bewiesen ist.[^fitzmaurice-family-carlow]

people.summary: Eliza Taylor of St Martin's parish, Birmingham. She married John FitzMaurice there on 3 February 1827. Mother of William, John Richard and Robert William.
people.story: Eliza Taylor, of the parish of St Martin's, Birmingham, married John FitzMaurice there by licence on 3 February 1827. John Taylor witnessed.[^parish-birmingham-1827] She is named with John at the baptisms of their three sons: William at St Mary's, Whitechapel, on 25 December 1827, John Richard at St Dunstan's, Stepney, on 4 November 1829, and Robert William at the same church on 30 September 1832.[^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] [^parish-stepney-1832] She was of Birmingham, which is probably why their son Robert William later settled there. Her birth and death have not been found.

people.story_de: Eliza Taylor, aus der Gemeinde St Martin's, Birmingham, heiratete John FitzMaurice dort am 3. Februar 1827 mit Lizenz. John Taylor war Trauzeuge.[^parish-birmingham-1827] Sie wird mit John bei den Taufen ihrer drei Söhne genannt: William in St Mary's, Whitechapel, am 25. Dezember 1827, John Richard in St Dunstan's, Stepney, am 4. November 1829 und Robert William in derselben Kirche am 30. September 1832.[^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] [^parish-stepney-1832] Sie stammte aus Birmingham, was wahrscheinlich der Grund dafür ist, dass ihr Sohn Robert William sich später dort niederließ. Ihre Geburt und ihr Tod sind nicht gefunden worden.

people.summary: Potter at Battersea, born abroad about 1793. Father of Fanny Mary. Buried at St Mary's, Battersea, on 27 August 1849, aged 56.
people.story: William Gottlob Falcke was born abroad about 1793. The 1841 census records him as a potter at Battersea, born in foreign parts.[^census-1841-falcke] He married Eliza Macfarlin at St Mary's, Battersea, on 15 October 1817. On their children's baptisms she is Elizabeth. They had ten children baptised at Chelsea and Battersea between 1818 and 1837. Fanny Mary, baptised in 1837, was the youngest.[^parish-falcke-1817] [^parish-battersea-1837] He was buried at St Mary's, Battersea, on 27 August 1849, aged 56.[^burial-falcke-1849] By 1861, when Fanny married, he was described as a manufacturer.[^parish-battersea-1861]

people.cardPlace: Mile End Old Town, then Birmingham
people.summary: Baptised 4 November 1829 at St Dunstan's, Stepney, son of John, a clerk in the Ordnance Office, and Eliza. In 1851 he was a surveyor lodging in Birmingham with his brother Robert William. By 1861 he was married to Anne, born in Guernsey, and living at Edgbaston, where in 1871, at Pershore Road, he gave his birthplace as the Tower of London.
people.story:
John Richard FitzMaurice was baptised on 4 November 1829 at St Dunstan's, Stepney, son of John and Eliza Fitzmaurice of Mile End Old Town. His father was a clerk in the Ordnance Office.[^parish-stepney-1829] The register gives the baptism, not a birth.

In 1851 he and his younger brother Robert William were lodging in William Street, in the Birmingham parish of St Thomas, in the house of Sarah Hill, a milliner. John R. was 21 and Robert W. 19, both unmarried, both surveyors, and both born in London. The enumerator wrote the surname as it sounded, and the index reads Fitzmansie.[^census-1851-birmingham-st-thomas] In 1861 John Richard was the head of his own household at Edgbaston, aged 33, married, born in Middlesex, London, and probably an assistant land surveyor (the first word is hard to read). His wife Anne, 34, was born in Guernsey.[^census-1861-edgbaston-jrf] In 1871 they lived at 367 Pershore Road, Edgbaston. John was 41, a land and road surveyor not in practice and an agent to the Birmingham Gas Company, as far as the entry can be read, and his birthplace was written as the Tower of London, which fits his father's post as an Ordnance clerk there. Annie, his wife, was 43 and born in Guernsey. A girl also named Annie, aged 4 and born in London, is entered as his niece, though one reading of the word gives daughter.[^census-1871-edgbaston-jrf]

openQuestions.question: When and where did he marry Anne, and who was she?
openQuestions.record: A marriage between 1851 and 1861; a Lambeth marriage of December quarter 1857 is a possible but unproved candidate.

openQuestions.question: Was Annie, aged 4 in 1871, his niece or his daughter, and when did John Richard die?
openQuestions.record: A London birth of an Annie Fitzmaurice about 1866 to 1867, and the death index after 1871.

people.summary_de: Getauft am 4. November 1829 in St Dunstan's, Stepney, Sohn von John, einem Schreiber im Ordnance Office, und Eliza. 1851 war er Landvermesser und wohnte mit seinem Bruder Robert William in Birmingham zur Untermiete. 1861 war er mit Anne verheiratet, die in Guernsey geboren war, und lebte in Edgbaston, wo er 1871 in der Pershore Road als Geburtsort den Tower of London angab.
people.story_de:
John Richard FitzMaurice wurde am 4. November 1829 in St Dunstan's, Stepney, getauft, Sohn von John und Eliza Fitzmaurice aus Mile End Old Town. Sein Vater war Schreiber im Ordnance Office.[^parish-stepney-1829] Das Register nennt die Taufe, keine Geburt.

1851 wohnten er und sein jüngerer Bruder Robert William in der William Street zur Untermiete, in der Pfarrei St Thomas in Birmingham, im Haus von Sarah Hill, einer Modistin. John R. war 21 und Robert W. 19, beide unverheiratet, beide Landvermesser und beide in London geboren. Der Zähler schrieb den Nachnamen so, wie er klang, und der Index lautet Fitzmansie.[^census-1851-birmingham-st-thomas] 1861 war John Richard Vorstand seines eigenen Haushalts in Edgbaston, 33 Jahre alt, verheiratet, geboren in Middlesex, London, und wahrscheinlich Landvermesserassistent (das erste Wort ist schwer zu lesen). Seine Frau Anne, 34 Jahre alt, wurde in Guernsey geboren.[^census-1861-edgbaston-jrf] 1871 lebten sie in 367 Pershore Road, Edgbaston. John war 41, ein nicht praktizierender Land- und Straßenvermesser und Agent der Birmingham Gas Company, soweit sich der Eintrag lesen lässt, und als Geburtsort war der Tower of London eingetragen, was zu der Stelle seines Vaters als Schreiber der Ordnance dort passt. Annie, seine Frau, war 43 und in Guernsey geboren. Ein Mädchen, ebenfalls Annie genannt, 4 Jahre alt und in London geboren, ist als seine Nichte eingetragen, obwohl eine Lesart des Wortes auf Tochter lautet.[^census-1871-edgbaston-jrf]

people.summary: Baptised 30 September 1832 at St Dunstan's, Stepney, son of John and Eliza. Surveyor, later a granite merchant and contractor. In 1879 he was a stone merchant in the Birmingham firm of Jones and Fitzmaurice, who probably opened the Cliffe Hill granite quarry at Markfield, Leicestershire. Married Fanny Mary Falcke in 1861. Died 10 May 1895 at Edgbaston.
people.story:
Robert William FitzMaurice was baptised on 30 September 1832 at St Dunstan's, Stepney, son of John, a clerk in the Tower, and Eliza. The date usually given as his birth is this baptism. He was the youngest of three sons. William was born in 1827 and John Richard was baptised in 1829.[^parish-stepney-1832] [^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] In 1851, aged 19, he was a surveyor lodging with his brother John Richard in William Street, Birmingham.[^census-1851-birmingham-st-thomas] On 14 September 1861, a surveyor, he married Fanny Mary Falcke at St Mary's, Battersea. His father John is called a gentleman on that register.[^parish-battersea-1861]

In 1871 he was a surveyor and contractor at Little Bromwich, Aston, born in Stepney.[^census-1871-aston] Kelly's Birmingham directory of 1879 lists Jones and Fitzmaurice, stone merchants, of Tindal Street, Ladywood, and Robt. Wm. Fitzmaurice, stone merchant, "see Jones & Fitzmaurice". The same directory has a Robert William Fitzmaurice living at Norlands, Erdington.[^kelly-1879-birmingham-jones-fitzmaurice] In 1881 he was a granite merchant and contractor at Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston] The published histories of the Cliffe Hill granite quarry, near Markfield in Leicestershire, say that quarrying there was begun in the 1870s by Mr Jones and Mr Fitzmaurice of Birmingham, who made setts and kerbs, and that they stopped in 1881. In 1891 J. Rupert Fitzmaurice acquired the quarry from his father and reopened it. That father was almost certainly Robert William, so he was probably the Fitzmaurice of Jones and Fitzmaurice.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history] [^mcgrath-2007-charnwood-quarries] The story of the quarry is on its own page. He died at Edgbaston on 10 May 1895, aged 64. His estate was 12,921 pounds 4 shillings and 9 pence. The executors were his widow Fanny Mary and their sons John Rupert, a quarry owner, and Walter, a contractor.[^probate-robert-1895] When his son Edward married in 1897, the register names Robert William Fitzmaurice, contractor, as the father, and says he was already dead.[^parish-brixton-1897]

people.summary_de: Getauft am 30. September 1832 in St Dunstan's, Stepney, Sohn von John und Eliza. Landvermesser, später Granithändler und Unternehmer. 1879 war er Steinhändler in der Birminghamer Firma Jones and Fitzmaurice, die wahrscheinlich den Granitsteinbruch Cliffe Hill in Markfield, Leicestershire, eröffnete. Heirat mit Fanny Mary Falcke 1861. Gestorben am 10. Mai 1895 in Edgbaston.
people.story_de:
Robert William FitzMaurice wurde am 30. September 1832 in St Dunstan's, Stepney, getauft, Sohn von John, einem Schreiber im Tower, und Eliza. Das Datum, das gewöhnlich als seine Geburt angegeben wird, ist diese Taufe. Er war der jüngste von drei Söhnen. William wurde 1827 geboren, und John Richard wurde 1829 getauft.[^parish-stepney-1832] [^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] 1851 war er, 19 Jahre alt, Landvermesser und wohnte mit seinem Bruder John Richard in der William Street, Birmingham, zur Untermiete.[^census-1851-birmingham-st-thomas] Am 14. September 1861 heiratete er als Landvermesser Fanny Mary Falcke in St Mary's, Battersea. Sein Vater John wird in diesem Register Gentleman genannt.[^parish-battersea-1861]

1871 war er Landvermesser und Unternehmer in Little Bromwich, Aston, geboren in Stepney.[^census-1871-aston] Kelly's Verzeichnis für Birmingham von 1879 führt Jones and Fitzmaurice, Steinhändler, in der Tindal Street, Ladywood, und Robt. Wm. Fitzmaurice, Steinhändler, "see Jones & Fitzmaurice". Dasselbe Verzeichnis führt einen Robert William Fitzmaurice in Norlands, Erdington.[^kelly-1879-birmingham-jones-fitzmaurice] 1881 war er Granithändler und Unternehmer in Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston] Die veröffentlichten Darstellungen des Granitsteinbruchs Cliffe Hill, bei Markfield in Leicestershire, besagen, dass der Abbau dort in den 1870er Jahren von Herrn Jones und Herrn Fitzmaurice aus Birmingham begonnen wurde, die Pflastersteine und Bordsteine herstellten, und dass sie 1881 aufhörten. 1891 erwarb J. Rupert Fitzmaurice den Steinbruch von seinem Vater und eröffnete ihn wieder. Dieser Vater war nahezu sicher Robert William, sodass er wahrscheinlich der Fitzmaurice von Jones and Fitzmaurice war.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history] [^mcgrath-2007-charnwood-quarries] Die Geschichte des Steinbruchs steht auf einer eigenen Seite. Er starb am 10. Mai 1895 in Edgbaston, 64 Jahre alt. Sein Nachlass betrug 12.921 Pfund, 4 Shilling und 9 Pence. Testamentsvollstrecker waren seine Witwe Fanny Mary und ihre Söhne John Rupert, Steinbruchbesitzer, und Walter, Unternehmer.[^probate-robert-1895] Als sein Sohn Edward 1897 heiratete, nennt das Register Robert William Fitzmaurice, Unternehmer, als Vater und vermerkt, dass er bereits tot war.[^parish-brixton-1897]

people.summary: Born 3 December 1836 and baptised 29 January 1837 at St Mary's, Battersea, youngest child of William Gottlob Falcke, potter, and Elizabeth. Died 25 October 1917 at Erdington.
people.story:
Fanny Mary was born on 3 December 1836 and baptised at St Mary's, Battersea, on 29 January 1837, as Mary Fanny, daughter of William Gottlob Falcke, a potter, and Elizabeth.[^parish-battersea-1837] She is in the family at Battersea in 1841 and, aged 14, with her mother in 1851.[^census-1841-falcke] [^census-1851-falcke] On 14 September 1861 she married Robert William FitzMaurice at the same church. The register calls her father a manufacturer.[^parish-battersea-1861]

A line in the 1871 census that gives her birthplace as France is a mistake. The baptism, the 1851 census and the 1881 census all give Battersea.[^census-1871-aston] [^census-1881-aston] She died at Erdington on 25 October 1917, aged 80.[^probate-fanny-1917] She was probably the mother of Edward Dixon: his birth index names the mother's maiden name as Falcke, and she was Robert William's wife.[^gro-indexes]
people.summary_de: Geboren am 3. Dezember 1836 und getauft am 29. Januar 1837 in St Mary's, Battersea, jüngstes Kind von William Gottlob Falcke, Töpfer, und Elizabeth. Gestorben am 25. Oktober 1917 in Erdington.
people.story_de:
Fanny Mary wurde am 3. Dezember 1836 geboren und am 29. Januar 1837 in St Mary's, Battersea, als Mary Fanny getauft, Tochter von William Gottlob Falcke, einem Töpfer, und Elizabeth.[^parish-battersea-1837] Sie ist 1841 bei der Familie in Battersea und 1851, 14 Jahre alt, bei ihrer Mutter.[^census-1841-falcke] [^census-1851-falcke] Am 14. September 1861 heiratete sie Robert William FitzMaurice in derselben Kirche. Das Register bezeichnet ihren Vater als Fabrikanten.[^parish-battersea-1861]

Eine Zeile der Volkszählung von 1871, die Frankreich als ihren Geburtsort angibt, ist ein Irrtum. Die Taufe, die Volkszählung von 1851 und die Volkszählung von 1881 geben alle Battersea an.[^census-1871-aston] [^census-1881-aston] Sie starb am 25. Oktober 1917 in Erdington, 80 Jahre alt.[^probate-fanny-1917] Sie war wahrscheinlich die Mutter von Edward Dixon: sein Geburtsindex nennt Falcke als Mädchennamen der Mutter, und sie war die Ehefrau von Robert William.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary: Probably a son of Robert William and Fanny Mary. Called Rupert J. in 1871. He acquired the Cliffe Hill granite quarry at Markfield from his father in 1891, reopened it, and the Cliffe Hill Granite Company was formed in 1894. A quarry owner in 1895, and one of his father's executors. Died at Leicester on 21 September 1949. He married Isabel Bennion in 1896 (she died in 1905) and Maria Adelaide Wood in 1907. His only son, John Herbert, was killed in France in 1918.
people.story:
John Rupert's birth was registered in the King's Norton district in the June quarter of 1865, volume 6c, page 447, mother's maiden name Falcke.[^gro-indexes] In 1871 he is the son recorded as Rupert J., aged 6, born in Birmingham.[^census-1871-aston] On 9 May 1891 J. Rupert Fitzmaurice acquired the Cliffe Hill granite quarry, near Markfield in Leicestershire, from his father, and reopened it, with Peter Preston as manager. The Cliffe Hill Granite Company Ltd was formed on 1 November 1894. The company bought the freehold of the quarry and its land from him in 1935.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history] [^mcgrath-2007-charnwood-quarries] [^graces-guide-cliffe-hill-granite] In 1895 he was a quarry owner and an executor of his father.[^probate-robert-1895] He died on 21 September 1949, aged 84, of 3 Salisbury Road, Leicester. The estate was 56,789 pounds 19 shillings and 2 pence.[^probate-rupert-1949] The quarry history also records the death of its original founder, J.R. Fitzmaurice, in 1949.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history]

He married Isabel Bennion in 1896, registered in the Lichfield district.[^freebmd-john-rupert-family-s51] In 1896 he signed letters to the Beaumanor estate as manager of the Cliffe Hill Granite Co.[^rollr-cliffe-hill-records] The quarry engine Isabel, delivered in 1897, was named after his wife.[^amerton-isabel] Their son John Herbert was born at Leicester in 1898 and a daughter, Mary Isabel, in 1899. Isabel died in 1905, aged 35, and in 1907 he married Maria Adelaide Wood at Petersham, Surrey. By 1911 the family lived at Cliveden, Manor Road, Oadby.[^oadby-remembers-jhf] John Herbert was killed in France in March 1918.[^cwgc-jhf-1918] In October 1937 J. R. Fitzmaurice, as chairman, signed the resolution to wind up Markfield Estates Ltd; the liquidator, Leslie Charlesworth Simpson, was later one of John Rupert's executors.[^gazette-1937-markfield-estates]

people.story_de:
Die Geburt von John Rupert wurde im Juniquartal 1865 im Registerbezirk King's Norton eingetragen, Band 6c, Seite 447, Mädchenname der Mutter Falcke.[^gro-indexes] 1871 ist er der als Rupert J. verzeichnete Sohn, 6 Jahre alt, geboren in Birmingham.[^census-1871-aston] Am 9. Mai 1891 erwarb J. Rupert Fitzmaurice den Granitsteinbruch Cliffe Hill bei Markfield in Leicestershire von seinem Vater und eröffnete ihn wieder, mit Peter Preston als Betriebsleiter. Die Cliffe Hill Granite Company Ltd wurde am 1. November 1894 gegründet. Die Gesellschaft kaufte ihm 1935 das freie Grundeigentum am Steinbruch und am zugehörigen Land ab.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history] [^mcgrath-2007-charnwood-quarries] [^graces-guide-cliffe-hill-granite] 1895 war er Steinbruchbesitzer und Testamentsvollstrecker seines Vaters.[^probate-robert-1895] Er starb am 21. September 1949, 84 Jahre alt, wohnhaft 3 Salisbury Road, Leicester. Der Nachlass betrug 56.789 Pfund, 19 Shilling und 2 Pence.[^probate-rupert-1949] Die Geschichte des Steinbruchs verzeichnet außerdem den Tod des ursprünglichen Gründers des Steinbruchs, J.R. Fitzmaurice, im Jahr 1949.[^mqp-cliffe-hill-history]

Er heiratete Isabel Bennion 1896, eingetragen im Registerbezirk Lichfield.[^freebmd-john-rupert-family-s51] 1896 unterzeichnete er Briefe an das Gut Beaumanor als Betriebsleiter der Cliffe Hill Granite Co.[^rollr-cliffe-hill-records] Die 1897 gelieferte Maschine Isabel des Steinbruchs wurde nach seiner Frau benannt.[^amerton-isabel] Ihr Sohn John Herbert wurde 1898 in Leicester geboren, und eine Tochter, Mary Isabel, 1899. R. Fitzmaurice als Vorsitzender den Beschluss, die Markfield Estates Ltd aufzulösen; der Liquidator Leslie Charlesworth Simpson war später einer der Testamentsvollstrecker von John Rupert.[^gazette-1937-markfield-estates]

The 1897 marriage register of his daughter Edith Madeline names him as her father and says he was already dead.[^parish-brixton-1897] Caroline, Edith's mother, was already a widow in April 1891, so he had died before then.[^census-1891-spencer] No death registration has been tied to him.
