Das Heiratsregister von 1897 seiner Tochter Edith Madeline nennt ihn als ihren Vater und gibt an, dass er bereits tot war.[^parish-brixton-1897] Caroline, Ediths Mutter, war im April 1891 bereits Witwe, er war also vorher gestorben.[^census-1891-spencer] Keine Sterbeeintragung wurde ihm zugeordnet.

people.summary: Mother of Edith Madeline. Born in Islington about 1847. A widow and lodging house keeper in 1891, and probably living with Edith and Edward in Brixton in 1901.
people.story: Caroline was Edith Madeline's mother. In 1891, a widow, she was a lodging house keeper at 15 Mornington Place, St Pancras (the house number may read 15b), born in Islington, aged 44, with her daughter Edith, a governess of 22.[^census-1891-spencer] She witnessed Edith's marriage in 1897.[^parish-brixton-1897] In 1901 she was probably living with Edith and Edward in Brixton, recorded as about 52.[^census-1901-brixton] The ages put her birth about 1843 to 1849, in Islington. An 1881 entry sometimes suggested for her has not been shown to be the same woman, and it is not used here. Her maiden name and her death have not been found.
people.summary_de: Mutter von Edith Madeline. Geboren in Islington um 1847. 1891 Witwe und Logierhauswirtin, und wahrscheinlich 1901 bei Edith und Edward in Brixton lebend.
people.story_de: Caroline war die Mutter von Edith Madeline. 1891 war sie, als Witwe, Logierhauswirtin in 15 Mornington Place, St Pancras (die Hausnummer könnte 15b lauten), geboren in Islington, 44 Jahre alt, mit ihrer Tochter Edith, einer Gouvernante von 22 Jahren.[^census-1891-spencer] Sie war Zeugin bei Ediths Heirat 1897.[^parish-brixton-1897] 1901 lebte sie wahrscheinlich bei Edith und Edward in Brixton, eingetragen mit etwa 52 Jahren.[^census-1901-brixton] Die Altersangaben legen ihre Geburt auf etwa 1843 bis 1849, in Islington. Ein Eintrag von 1881, der bisweilen für sie angeführt wird, ist nicht als dieselbe Frau nachgewiesen, und er wird hier nicht verwendet. Ihr Mädchenname und ihr Tod wurden nicht gefunden.

people.summary: Reg's elder sister, named after her mother. Probably born in late 1899 in the Greenwich district, and died the next summer in the Lewisham district, under a year old.
people.story: Edith Marjorie Fitzmaurice, mother's maiden name Spencer, was registered in the Greenwich district in the December quarter of 1899, volume 1d, page 1075.[^gro-indexes] She died in the September quarter of 1900 in the Lewisham district, volume 1d, page 707, aged under a year.[^gro-indexes] The 1911 census says four children had been born to Edward and Edith and one had died. She is that child.[^census-1911-whitstable] She did not grow up, so she is not the woman in the medallion portrait.

people.story_de: Edith Marjorie Fitzmaurice, Mädchenname der Mutter Spencer, wurde im Dezemberquartal 1899 im Registerbezirk Greenwich eingetragen, Band 1d, Seite 1075.[^gro-indexes] Sie starb im Septemberquartal 1900 im Registerbezirk Lewisham, Band 1d, Seite 707, im Alter von unter einem Jahr.[^gro-indexes] Die Volkszählung von 1911 gibt an, dass vier Kinder von Edward und Edith geboren worden waren und eines gestorben war. Sie ist dieses Kind.[^census-1911-whitstable] Sie wuchs nicht heran, daher ist sie nicht die Frau auf dem Medaillonbildnis.

people.summary: Reg's younger sister, called Auntie Babs (confirmed by the family). Born late 1907 in the Blean district of Kent, daughter of Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline. She probably sailed to Cape Town in 1916, married Leslie Hugh Simmons at Staines in the summer of 1936, and probably died at Canterbury in early 1996.
people.story:
The youngest of Edward Dixon and Edith's children, Eileen was 3 at Whitstable in 1911.[^census-1911-whitstable] She was probably the girl of 8 who sailed to Cape Town with her mother and brothers in August 1916.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] She came back to London from South Africa with her mother and Reg on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, aged 16.[^passenger-1923-bendigo] A snapshot of a girl on a verandah is labelled on the back Auntie Babs, South Africa, and the letters Eil are scratched into the front. The family confirms she was that girl.[^photo-labels] [^beach-snapshots]

She married Leslie Hugh Simmons, secretary of the Corinth Hockey Club, at Staines in the summer of 1936. The local paper called her the daughter of the late Mr Edward Dixon Fitzmaurice, formerly of Cape Town.[^news-1936-simmons] In 1939 the couple lived at Hayes, close to her brother Reg. Leslie was a rate fixer and motion study engineer.[^register-1939] As Auntie Babs she was at Pat's wedding in 1950, with Uncle Leslie beside her.[^album-1950]

In 1984 she married Ralph Hallawell in Kent, and she probably died at Canterbury in early 1996, aged 88.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary_de: Regs jüngere Schwester, genannt Auntie Babs (von der Familie bestätigt). Ende 1907 im Registerbezirk Blean in Kent geboren, Tochter von Edward Dixon und Edith Madeline. Sie fuhr wahrscheinlich 1916 nach Kapstadt, heiratete Leslie Hugh Simmons im Sommer 1936 in Staines und starb wahrscheinlich Anfang 1996 in Canterbury.
people.story_de:
Als jüngstes der Kinder von Edward Dixon und Edith war Eileen 1911 in Whitstable 3 Jahre alt.[^census-1911-whitstable] Sie war wahrscheinlich das achtjährige Mädchen, das im August 1916 mit ihrer Mutter und den Brüdern nach Kapstadt fuhr.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] Sie kehrte mit ihrer Mutter und Reg auf der Bendigo aus Südafrika nach London zurück und kam am 28. Dezember 1923 an, 16 Jahre alt.[^passenger-1923-bendigo] Ein Schnappschuss eines Mädchens auf einer Veranda trägt auf der Rückseite die Beschriftung Auntie Babs, South Africa, und auf der Vorderseite sind die Buchstaben Eil eingeritzt. Die Familie bestätigt, dass sie dieses Mädchen war.[^photo-labels] [^beach-snapshots]

Sie heiratete Leslie Hugh Simmons, Schriftführer des Corinth Hockey Club, im Sommer 1936 in Staines. Die Lokalzeitung nannte sie die Tochter des verstorbenen Mr Edward Dixon Fitzmaurice, früher in Kapstadt ansässig.[^news-1936-simmons] 1939 lebte das Paar in Hayes, nahe bei ihrem Bruder Reg. Leslie war Lohnsatzfestsetzer und Ingenieur für Bewegungsstudien.[^register-1939] Als Auntie Babs war sie 1950 auf Pats Hochzeit, mit Uncle Leslie an ihrer Seite.[^album-1950]

1984 heiratete sie Ralph Hallawell in Kent, und sie starb wahrscheinlich Anfang 1996 in Canterbury, 88 Jahre alt.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary: Lilian's father. A tailor, later a general labourer, then a tailor and outfitter, born at Egloshayle in Cornwall about 1850. He and Annie were living apart in 1911. He probably died at Bodmin on 5 December 1925, aged 77.
people.story:
Charles Bennett was born at Egloshayle, Cornwall, about 1849 to 1851. In 1891 he was a tailor in Bodmin. In 1901 he was a general labourer at 1 Honey Street, Bodmin. In 1911 he was 62, a tailor and outfitter, born at Slades, Egloshayle, and living in Bodmin with his son Frank.[^census-bennett] He and Annie had probably married in 1882, in the Stoke Damerel district.[^gro-bennett-grigg]

In 1911 they were living apart in the same town. Annie, who kept a draper's shop, described herself as a widow, but Charles was alive. Both of their census forms say 11 children had been born, 8 were living and 3 had died.[^census-bennett] He probably died at Bodmin on 5 December 1925, aged 77. Administration of his estate, 296 pounds 1 shilling and 4 pence, was granted to May Bennett, a spinster. That grant does not, by itself, show which daughter she was.[^probate-charles-bennett-1926]

people.summary_de: Lilians Vater. Schneider, später allgemeiner Arbeiter, dann Schneider und Ausstatter, geboren in Egloshayle in Cornwall um 1850. Er und Annie lebten 1911 getrennt. Er starb wahrscheinlich am 5. Dezember 1925 in Bodmin, 77 Jahre alt.
people.story_de:
Charles Bennett wurde in Egloshayle, Cornwall, etwa 1849 bis 1851 geboren. 1891 war er Schneider in Bodmin. 1901 war er allgemeiner Arbeiter in 1 Honey Street, Bodmin. 1911 war er 62, Schneider und Ausstatter, geboren in Slades, Egloshayle, und lebte in Bodmin mit seinem Sohn Frank.[^census-bennett] Er und Annie hatten wahrscheinlich 1882 im Registerbezirk Stoke Damerel geheiratet.[^gro-bennett-grigg]

1911 lebten sie in derselben Stadt getrennt. Annie, die ein Tuchgeschäft führte, bezeichnete sich als Witwe, doch Charles war am Leben. Auf beiden Volkszählungsformularen steht, dass 11 Kinder geboren worden waren, 8 lebten und 3 gestorben waren.[^census-bennett] Er starb wahrscheinlich am 5. Dezember 1925 in Bodmin, 77 Jahre alt. Die Verwaltung seines Nachlasses, 296 Pfund, 1 Shilling und 4 Pence, wurde May Bennett, ledig, erteilt. Diese Erteilung zeigt für sich allein nicht, welche Tochter sie war.[^probate-charles-bennett-1926]

people.summary: Lilian's mother, probably Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg, known as Annie. Born in the St Columb district about 1864. A draper by 1911. Died at Bodmin in 1912, aged 48.
people.story: Annie, Lilian's mother, was probably Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg, born in the St Columb district in the March quarter of 1864, volume 5c, page 131, mother's maiden name Stephens.[^gro-bennett-grigg] The censuses call her Annie, born at St Columb. In 1891 and 1901 she is Charles Bennett's wife in Bodmin. In 1911 she kept a draper's shop and described herself as a widow, although Charles was alive in the same town. Her form says she had been married 28 years, with 11 children born, 8 living and 3 dead.[^census-bennett] She died in the June quarter of 1912 at Bodmin, aged 48, registered as Matilda Ann Nicholls Bennett, volume 5c, page 89.[^gro-bennett-grigg]
people.summary_de: Lilians Mutter, wahrscheinlich Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg, bekannt als Annie. Geboren im Registerbezirk St Columb um 1864. 1911 Tuchhändlerin. Gestorben 1912 in Bodmin, 48 Jahre alt.
people.story_de: Annie, Lilians Mutter, war wahrscheinlich Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg, geboren im Registerbezirk St Columb im Märzquartal 1864, Band 5c, Seite 131, Mädchenname der Mutter Stephens.[^gro-bennett-grigg] Die Volkszählungen nennen sie Annie, geboren in St Columb. 1891 und 1901 ist sie die Ehefrau von Charles Bennett in Bodmin. 1911 führte sie ein Tuchgeschäft und bezeichnete sich als Witwe, obwohl Charles in derselben Stadt noch am Leben war. Ihr Formular gibt an, sie sei seit 28 Jahren verheiratet gewesen, mit 11 geborenen Kindern, 8 lebenden und 3 toten.[^census-bennett] Sie starb im Juniquartal 1912 in Bodmin, 48 Jahre alt, eingetragen als Matilda Ann Nicholls Bennett, Band 5c, Seite 89.[^gro-bennett-grigg]

people.summary: Father of Lucy's father. An agricultural labourer at Denham, Buckinghamshire. Probably born about 1801 to 1806.
people.story: Henry Stacey, an agricultural labourer, is at Denham in the 1841 census with his wife Ann and their children, including a son Henry aged 7, who is Lucy's father. The 1841 age of 35 was often rounded. The 1851 census gives him as about 47 and born at Chalfont, Buckinghamshire, so he was probably born about 1801 to 1806.[^census-andrews-stacey] [^parish-denham-1834]

Das Alter von 35 im Jahr 1841 wurde oft gerundet. Die Volkszählung von 1851 gibt ihn mit etwa 47 Jahren an und als geboren in Chalfont, Buckinghamshire, sodass er wahrscheinlich etwa 1801 bis 1806 geboren wurde.[^census-andrews-stacey] [^parish-denham-1834]

people.summary: Lucy's father. Baptised at Denham on 16 March 1834, son of Henry and Ann. A farm labourer. Married Mary Walter at Leavesden on 5 June 1858.
people.story:
Henry Stacey was baptised at Denham, Buckinghamshire, on 16 March 1834, son of Henry and Ann.[^parish-denham-1834] He is the boy of 7 in the family at Denham in 1841.[^census-andrews-stacey] On 5 June 1858 he married Mary Walter at Leavesden. He gave his age as 24. Later censuses and the baptism agree better with 1834, so the marriage age was probably a little high.[^parish-leavesden-1858]

He was a farm labourer. In 1861 he and Mary, with their first child Emily, were visiting at Abbots Langley. In 1871 the family was at Aldenham, and Lucy was 6. In 1881 and 1891 they were at Bushey.[^census-andrews-stacey]

Juni 1858 heiratete er Mary Walter in Leavesden. Er gab sein Alter mit 24 an. Spätere Volkszählungen und die Taufe passen besser zu 1834, sodass das Heiratsalter wahrscheinlich etwas zu hoch war.[^parish-leavesden-1858]

Er war Landarbeiter. 1861 waren er und Mary mit ihrem ersten Kind Emily zu Besuch in Abbots Langley. 1871 war die Familie in Aldenham, und Lucy war 6. 1881 und 1891 waren sie in Bushey.[^census-andrews-stacey]

The later censuses agree with a birth in 1838.[^parish-leavesden-1858] Lucy's birth index names the mother's maiden name as Walter, so Mary was Lucy's mother.[^parish-leavesden-1858]

people.summary: Ron's grandfather. A journeyman baker, born at Totternhoe. The 1939 Register gives 12 November 1865. Married Lucy Stacey at Bushey on 17 May 1888. Probably died in early 1951.
people.story:
Herbert Andrews was born at Totternhoe, Bedfordshire. He was 5 there in 1871, son of George and Alice.[^census-andrews-stacey] At 15 he was probably a page in a household at Wimbledon.[^census-andrews-stacey] On 17 May 1888, aged 22, he married Lucy Stacey at Bushey. His father is named as George Andrews.[^parish-bushey-1888]

He worked as a journeyman baker: at Hemel Hempstead in 1901, at Canning Town in 1911, and on night work for a bakery in Plymouth Road, Canning Town, in 1921, when he and Lucy were at Plaistow.[^census-andrews-stacey] Henry George was their only child.[^census-andrews-stacey] The 1939 Register gives his birth as 12 November 1865 and calls him a retired baker and a widower, at West Ham.[^register-1939] He probably died in the March quarter of 1951 in the Essex South Western district, volume 5a, page 209, aged 84. That age is about a year younger than the 1939 birth date.[^gro-indexes]

people.story_de:
Herbert Andrews wurde in Totternhoe, Bedfordshire, geboren. 1871 war er dort 5 Jahre alt, Sohn von George und Alice.[^census-andrews-stacey] Mit 15 war er wahrscheinlich Page in einem Haushalt in Wimbledon.[^census-andrews-stacey] Am 17. Mai 1888, im Alter von 22 Jahren, heiratete er Lucy Stacey in Bushey. Sein Vater wird als George Andrews genannt.[^parish-bushey-1888]

Er arbeitete als Bäckergeselle: 1901 in Hemel Hempstead, 1911 in Canning Town und 1921 in Nachtarbeit für eine Bäckerei in Plymouth Road, Canning Town, als er und Lucy in Plaistow waren.[^census-andrews-stacey] Henry George war ihr einziges Kind.[^census-andrews-stacey] Das Register von 1939 gibt seine Geburt mit dem 12. November 1865 an und bezeichnet ihn als Bäcker im Ruhestand und als Witwer, in West Ham.[^register-1939] Er starb wahrscheinlich im Märzquartal 1951 im Bezirk Essex South Western, Band 5a, Seite 209, im Alter von 84 Jahren. Dieses Alter ist etwa ein Jahr jünger als das Geburtsdatum von 1939.[^gro-indexes]

people.story:
Lucy Stacey was born in the June quarter of 1865 in the Watford district, volume 3a, page 333, mother's maiden name Walter.[^parish-leavesden-1858] She was 6 at Aldenham in 1871, daughter of Henry and Mary, and the censuses give her birthplace as Watford and, later, Leavesden.[^census-andrews-stacey] In 1881 she was a general servant at Watford, aged 16.[^census-andrews-stacey] She married Herbert Andrews at Bushey on 17 May 1888.[^parish-bushey-1888]

Henry George was their only child: the 1911 census says one child born and one living.[^census-andrews-stacey] She probably died in the September quarter of 1932 in the West Ham district, volume 4a, page 153, aged 67.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary: Rosina's father. Probably baptised on 1 December 1850 at St John, Hackney, son of William Cousins and Elizabeth. A clerk in 1871, later a wharf foreman and a dock labourer. Probably died in the West Ham district in late 1922, aged 71.
people.story:
William Cousins was probably baptised on 1 December 1850 at St John, Hackney, the son of William Cousins, a porter, and his wife Elizabeth.[^parish-hackney-1850] In 1861 the family was probably living at Mile End Old Town. His father was a messenger, and the children included a sister Amelia.[^census-1861-cousins]

On 15 January 1871, aged 21 and a clerk, he married Anne Gall at St Philip's, Stepney. The register names his father as William Cousins, a clerk.[^parish-stepney-1871] In 1881 he was a wharf foreman in Bermondsey. The later censuses take the family to West Ham. By 1901 Annie had died, and he was in Canning Town with Amelia and Herbert. In 1911 and 1921 he was at Plaistow, in 1921 a retired dock labourer in the household of his daughter Rosina and her husband Henry George.[^census-cousins]

He is named as Rosina's father on her marriage in 1915.[^parish-plaistow-1915] He probably died in the December quarter of 1922 in the West Ham district, volume 4a, page 53, aged 71.[^gro-cousins-gall]

people.story_de:
William Cousins wurde wahrscheinlich am 1. Dezember 1850 in St John, Hackney, getauft, als Sohn von William Cousins, einem Träger, und seiner Frau Elizabeth.[^parish-hackney-1850] 1861 lebte die Familie wahrscheinlich in Mile End Old Town. Sein Vater war Bote, und zu den Kindern gehörte eine Schwester Amelia.[^census-1861-cousins]

Am 15. Januar 1871, 21 Jahre alt und Kontorist, heiratete er Anne Gall in St Philip's, Stepney. Das Register nennt seinen Vater als William Cousins, Kontorist.[^parish-stepney-1871] 1881 war er Vorarbeiter am Kai in Bermondsey. Er wird bei ihrer Heirat 1915 als Vater von Rosina genannt.[^parish-plaistow-1915] Er starb wahrscheinlich im Dezemberquartal 1922 im Bezirk West Ham, Band 4a, Seite 53, im Alter von 71 Jahren.[^gro-cousins-gall]

people.story:
Annie Cousins was born Anne Gall. She was the daughter of John Gall, a brewer, who had died before she married. On 15 January 1871, aged 24, she married William Cousins at St Philip's, Stepney.[^parish-stepney-1871] The birth index gives the mother's maiden name as Gall for all eight of their children, so the maiden name is certain.[^gro-cousins-gall]

The censuses say she was born at Thetford, Norfolk, about 1846.[^census-cousins] She had died before the 1901 census. She probably died in the September quarter of 1900 in the West Ham district, volume 4a, page 76, aged 53.[^gro-cousins-gall]

people.summary: Auntie May. Rosina's younger sister, born in the spring of 1886 in the West Ham district. She never married. She lived at Chiswick, and died on 27 September 1971.
people.story:
May Florence Cousins, mother's maiden name Gall, was registered in the West Ham district in the June quarter of 1886, volume 4a, page 167.[^census-1921-may] She never married. In 1921 she was 35, a ward maid at East Ham Isolation Hospital. She later worked at Ealing, and in 1939 she was a dining hall maid at Colchester.[^census-1921-may] [^register-1939] From 1948 to 1967 the electoral registers place her at Chiswick and Gunnersbury, and then at Feltham.[^electoral-may] She died on 27 September 1971. The estate was 1,541 pounds.[^probate-may-1971]

This is the Auntie May Amanda remembered: an elderly aunt who had never married, who came to stay, and who lived at Chiswick. She was probably also the Auntie May named at Pat and Ron's wedding, though that last step is not proved. Lilian's sister Minnie is a different person.

people.story_de:
May Florence Cousins, Mädchenname der Mutter Gall, wurde im Juniquartal 1886 im Bezirk West Ham registriert, Band 4a, Seite 167.[^census-1921-may] Sie hat nie geheiratet. 1921 war sie 35, Stationsmädchen im East Ham Isolation Hospital. Später arbeitete sie in Ealing, und 1939 war sie Speisesaalmädchen in Colchester.[^census-1921-may] [^register-1939] Von 1948 bis 1967 führen die Wählerverzeichnisse sie in Chiswick und Gunnersbury, und danach in Feltham.[^electoral-may] Sie starb am 27. September 1971. Der Nachlass betrug 1541 Pfund.[^probate-may-1971]

Dies ist die Auntie May, an die sich Amanda erinnerte: eine ältere Tante, die nie geheiratet hatte, die zu Besuch kam und die in Chiswick lebte. Sie war wahrscheinlich auch die Auntie May, die bei der Hochzeit von Pat und Ron genannt wurde, auch wenn dieser letzte Schritt nicht bewiesen ist. Lilians Schwester Minnie ist eine andere Person.

people.summary: Probably the only son of John Rupert FitzMaurice and his first wife Isabel. Born at Leicester in 1898. He served in France with the 6th King's Shropshire Light Infantry, was reported missing near St Quentin on 25 March 1918, and is named on the Pozieres Memorial on the Somme; he was at Shrewsbury School until 1916 and is not shown at the 1916 Battle of the Somme.
people.story:
John Herbert's birth was registered at Leicester in the September quarter of 1898.[^freebmd-john-rupert-family-s51] Oadby Remembers gives his birth date as 23 June 1898, his parents as John Rupert Fitzmaurice and Isabel, nee Bennion, and his baptism at St Mary's, Weeford, Staffordshire, on 9 August 1898. It says the family lived in Westcotes Drive, Leicester, in 1901 and at Cliveden, Manor Road, Oadby, by 1911, and that he was at Shrewsbury School from 1912 to 1916.[^oadby-remembers-jhf] His mother died in 1905, and her gravestone at Sutton Coldfield calls him "her only son".[^iwm-memorial-68733]

The London Gazette of 20 November 1917 lists him among the cadets made temporary second lieutenants on 31 October 1917, in the Shropshire Light Infantry,[^gazette-1917-30390-jhf] and that of 7 February 1918 transfers him to a service battalion from the same date.[^gazette-1918-30513-jhf] He was a second lieutenant in the 6th Battalion when he died on active service on 25 March 1918, during the German spring offensive. He has no known grave and is named on the Pozieres Memorial on the Somme. He was at Shrewsbury School from 1912 to 1916 and was commissioned only in 1917, so the records do not show him at the 1916 Battle of the Somme.[^cwgc-jhf-1918] He is also named on the war memorials at Oadby[^iwm-memorial-37741] and at St Mary Magdalene, Knighton.[^iwm-memorial-37773] His officer's file survives at The National Archives.[^tna-wo339-108430]

people.summary_de: Wahrscheinlich der einzige Sohn von John Rupert FitzMaurice und seiner ersten Frau Isabel. Geboren 1898 in Leicester. Er diente in Frankreich beim 6th King's Shropshire Light Infantry, wurde am 25. März 1918 in der Nähe von St Quentin als vermisst gemeldet und wird auf dem Pozieres Memorial an der Somme genannt; er war bis 1916 an der Shrewsbury School und wird bei der Schlacht an der Somme 1916 nicht aufgeführt.
people.story_de:
John Herberts Geburt wurde im Septemberquartal 1898 in Leicester registriert.[^freebmd-john-rupert-family-s51] Oadby Remembers gibt sein Geburtsdatum mit dem 23. Juni 1898 an, seine Eltern als John Rupert Fitzmaurice und Isabel, geborene Bennion, und seine Taufe in St Mary's, Weeford, Staffordshire, am 9. August 1898. Es sagt, die Familie habe 1901 in Westcotes Drive, Leicester, und spätestens 1911 in Cliveden, Manor Road, Oadby, gelebt, und er sei von 1912 bis 1916 an der Shrewsbury School gewesen.[^oadby-remembers-jhf] Seine Mutter starb 1905, und ihr Grabstein in Sutton Coldfield nennt ihn "her only son".[^iwm-memorial-68733]

Die London Gazette vom 20. November 1917 führt ihn unter den Kadetten auf, die am 31. Oktober 1917 zu zeitweiligen Leutnanten ernannt wurden, in der Shropshire Light Infantry,[^gazette-1917-30390-jhf] und die vom 7. Februar 1918 versetzt ihn ab demselben Datum zu einem Service Battalion.[^gazette-1918-30513-jhf] Er war Leutnant im 6th Battalion, als er am 25. März 1918 im aktiven Dienst während der deutschen Frühjahrsoffensive starb. Er hat kein bekanntes Grab und wird auf dem Pozieres Memorial an der Somme genannt. Er war von 1912 bis 1916 an der Shrewsbury School und erhielt erst 1917 sein Offizierspatent, sodass die Unterlagen ihn bei der Schlacht an der Somme 1916 nicht zeigen.[^cwgc-jhf-1918] Er wird auch auf den Kriegerdenkmälern in Oadby[^iwm-memorial-37741] und in St Mary Magdalene, Knighton, genannt.[^iwm-memorial-37773] Seine Offiziersakte ist in The National Archives überliefert.[^tna-wo339-108430]
